385YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for Astolat, Bregasland, Holberg, Karsk, Mournwold, Reikos, Segura and Semmerholm. The Senate appointed generals for seven armies, including Isaella's Dance, the Bloodcloaks and the Tusks, along with ambassadors to Faraden, Otkodov, the Commonwealth and the Sumaah Republic, and Bernard Dugdale as Imperial Spymaster. The Synod chose Jared as Lepidean Librarian with 363 votes, among other judgements, and cardinals named gatekeepers and a Chaplain Consular. Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo became Imperial Fleet Master. Bourse auctions and votes allocated seats such as the Master of the Imperial Mint and the Marracossa Sendito. The Imperial titles list was updated with these results.

n.Dawn: Dawn returned two senators: Bohemond De Rondell for Astolat and Amicia of the Semmerlak for Semmerholm.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Reikos elected Cyrus, of Ebon's Hall as its senator.
n.Jotun: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold was returned as senator for Bregasland, a territory then held by the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast elected Diego i Del Toro i Erigo as senator for Segura.
n.The League: The League returned Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg as senator for Holberg.
n.The Marches: The Marches elected Willum of Goatsbridge as senator for Mournwold.
n.Varushka: Varushka returned Yegor as senator for Karsk.

t.Astolat: Bohemond De Rondell was elected Senator for Astolat.
t.Bregasland: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold was elected Senator for Bregasland, while the territory was held by the Jotun.
t.Holberg: Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg was elected Senator for Holberg.
t.Karsk: Yegor was elected Senator for Karsk.
t.Mournwold: Willum of Goatsbridge was elected Senator for Mournwold.
t.Reikos: Cyrus, of Ebon's Hall was elected Senator for Reikos.
t.Segura: Diego i Del Toro i Erigo was elected Senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Amicia of the Semmerlak was elected Senator for Semmerholm.

385YE Spring Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1990 thrones. The Senate ratified the treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact and declared war on Asavea, making the Asavean Archipelago barbarians. It disbursed 500 thrones to Morrow for military resupply and moved the Master of Works to the Military Council. The Urdur spy network was approved, then abrogated. Funded commissions included the Smokehouse of Atalaq (215 thrones), the roads of Kahraman (200) and support for Caitun (70). Further works were announced, including a Temeschwar mana exchange and the Steel Rings of Sarvos. Appointments included Bernard Dugdale as Imperial Spymaster and ambassadors to the Sumaah Republic, the Commonwealth, Otkodov and the Faraden. The Constitutional Court ruled that an ambassador's election season cannot simply be moved.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained the Barrens as a Dawnish territory able to appoint a senator, on a motion proposed by the senator for Astolat.
n.Druj: The Barrens, held by the Druj that season, were assigned by the Senate to Dawn.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a failed naval supply appraisal hoped to avoid technically breaking the Grendel treaty.
n.Highguard: Highborn senators amended the Witness of Conclave's duties and the Sevenfold Path's manifesto, and the Necropolis senator proposed the Throne election, which elected nobody.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind gained the Palace of Flowers folly, ceded to the Yerende sept, and the announced Kragg's Hollow mana sinecure, while the Lepidean Library was set to research Jaggah, mother of Thrace.
n.Jotun: Jotun-held Bregasland was assigned to the Marches, and the Smokehouse of Atalaq was commissioned to help Sermersuaq recover from Jotun invasion.
n.Navarr: Navarr gained a House of Healing and the Garden of Glory in Therunin, and the Hall of the Seven was announced in Miaren, creating the Spear of the Seven.
n.The Brass Coast: The Madruga senator's motion to declare war on Asavea passed, and the roads of Kahraman are to be rebuilt with Kamkrag, with 200 thrones of support.
n.The League: The League saw the Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, the Steel Rings of Sarvos and the Anvil Library Scriptorium announced, but the Holberg cascade and Temeschwar University funding failed. Two citizens of Tassato became ambassadors.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained Bregasland as a Marcher territory, and Lowther's Lift was commissioned in Mournwold to extract more mithril.
n.Urizen: Morrow received 500 thrones for military resupply, the Gardens of Pallas in Zenith are to be appraised, and the Academy of Arms expansion passed.
n.Varushka: Ossium is to be appraised for lifting the under-threat status of Echofell and the Drownbark Forest. Fania Vessely-Vanek became Ambassador to Otkodov, and Varushkan senators raised and then abrogated the Urdur spy network.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a runeforge in Hahnmark, plus the Smokehouse of Atalaq and Hall of the Hunters in Sermersuaq, and Kallavesa secured support for the Faraden expansion of Caitun.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed assigning the Barrens to Dawn and seconded the Garden of Glory commission.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the failed Holberg cascade and seconded the Witness of Conclave amendment.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland was assigned to the Marches and can now appoint a senator, who proposed the election of the Ambassador to the Faraden.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed amending the Sevenfold Path's manifesto and seconded the withdrawn Hall of the Seven motion.
t.Hahnmark: A runeforge was commissioned in Hahnmark, tied to the Snow might fall wind of fortune.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Imperial Spymaster election and seconded the unsuccessful Throne election.
t.Holberg: A self-funded mana sinecure, Holberg's Melodious Cascade in Holmaeur, failed to pass, though Holberg's senator successfully proposed ratifying the Kaliact treaty.
t.Kahraman: The roads of Kahraman are to be rebuilt, with Kamkrag across the territory for troop movement and defence, with 200 thrones from the treasury.
t.Kallavesa: Wittal Grove's healing house will grow cerulean mazzarine, and Kallavesa's senator secured 70 thrones to send weirwood for the expansion of Caitun.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Urdur spy network, later abrogated, and seconded the Orieb improvement.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded abrogating the Urdur spy network and proposed the Ambassador to Otkodov election.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the successful declaration of war on Asavea and seconded the Academy of Arms expansion.
t.Miaren: The Hall of the Seven ministry was announced in Miaren, creating the Spear of the Seven to explore Terunael ruins held by the vallorn.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded the declaration of war on Asavea and proposed a failed naval supply appraisal.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed Lowther's Lift in Mournwold and seconded support for Caitun.
t.Morrow: The senator for Morrow received 500 thrones for military resupply.
t.Mournwold: Lowther's Lift was commissioned in the Singing Caves near Overton to extract greater quantities of mithril.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Throne election, which elected nobody, and seconded the Master of Works amendment.
t.Ossium: An appraisal of removing the under-threat quality from Echofell and the Drownbark Forest is due by Summer, and an improvement of Orieb in the Drownbark passed but will not begin.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Academy of Arms expansion and seconded ratifying the Kaliact treaty.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Witness of Conclave amendment and seconded the House of Healing.
t.Sarvos: The Steel Rings of Sarvos were announced to protect Sarvos from naval attack, and the Anvil Library Scriptorium will be built in Rodez, Foracci.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed abrogating the Urdur spy network and seconded a failed naval appraisal.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the ambassador election-season amendment and seconded the Gardens of Pallas appraisal.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq received 215 thrones for the Smokehouse of Atalaq to restore its farms and hunters, and the Hall of the Hunters was announced at Lake Atkonaroq.
t.Skarsind: The Palace of Flowers folly in Solvihill will be ceded to the Yerende sept, and Kragg's Hollow was announced as a mana sinecure.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: a failed Black Canal appraisal named Tassato as a preferred site, and its senator proposed the Garden of Glory.
t.Temeschwar: The Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange was announced in Hanuri, but funds for the University Department of Architecture failed and the Master of Rings title was amended.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens were assigned to Dawn and can now appoint a senator.
t.Therunin: Therunin gained the House of Healing, creating the Hand of the Healing, and the Garden of Glory liao sinecure, overseen by the Navarr National Assembly.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the failed Black Canal appraisal and seconded the assignment of Bregasland to the Marches.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: its senator proposed the Orieb improvement and seconded the rebuilding of Kahraman's roads.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: its senator seconded a failed appraisal on increasing Imperial navies.
t.Zenith: The Gardens of Pallas in Zenith are to be appraised for restoration, and Zenith's senator moved the Master of Works to the Military Council.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Healing House of Wittal Grove will grow cerulean mazzarine until its Grimnir announces otherwise.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: The Anvil Library Scriptorium, a liao and Synod-vote sinecure, is to be built in Rodez in Foracci.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Hall of the Hunters sinecure was announced at Lake Atkonaroq, creating the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, a mana ministry overseen by the Keeper of the Tome, was announced in Hanuri.

385YE Spring Equinox interlude.d: The League and Varushkan assemblies urged the destruction of the Vyig, opening an adventure for League, Imperial Orc and Varushkan military units. Rising Wolf activity in Varushka created paid monster-hunting work for Varushkan and Dawnish forces. The Imperial Guerdon stood at 350 thrones, shared among six named armies. Free Folk visits gave every congregation 36 extra rings but removed earlier liao and vote bonuses in five territories. Highguard businesses suffered to fund Free Folk tutelage. Tharim's Black Frost withered Dawnish farms and mana sites in return for aid against the Barrens. Hallow of the Green World was cast, Thunderous Tread of the Trees struck Liathaven, and Regrow the Land's Heart was cast in Madruga. Two rituals entered Imperial lore.

n.Dawn: Tharim's Black Frost cost every Dawnish farm 36 rings and every mana site one crystal until the Autumn Equinox, in exchange for steel-bound knights to aid any Dawnish army attacking the Barrens. Dawnish knights-errant could also seek glory hunting monsters in Varushka.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel held Feroz, where Imperial fleets could support the Osseini spy network.
n.Highguard: Highborn congregations gained extra liao, two Synod votes and a crown of income from the Birthplace of the Way. Every Highguard business suffered a -1 rank production penalty to fund tutelage of Free Folk priests.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc thief-takers were among those hired against the Vyig, and Imperial Orc military units could join the Break the Vyig adventure.
n.Jotun: Thunderous Tread of the Trees was cast in Liathaven, where possessed plants attack armies and fortifications, and the Jotun there were expected to bear the brunt.
n.Navarr: At the national assembly's welcome, Great Forest Orcs settled in Miaren and Hercynia, aiding weirwood groves. Navarr herb gardens in four territories could be improved for one wain less weirwood until the Summer Solstice.
n.The Brass Coast: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast in Madruga to help contain the desiccating blight on the Great Grasses.
n.The League: The League assembly enacted a mandate to destroy the Vyig, funding bounty hunters and opening an adventure for military units. League Ambition congregations gained extra liao and votes, Holberg farms received Sand Fisher herbs, and Tassato and Temeschwar lost earlier congregation bonuses.
n.Urizen: Urizen congregations shared in the Free Folk donations, but Redoubt lost its earlier extra liao and votes. New rituals had also been added to Urizen lore.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly joined the mandate against the Vyig, and growing Wolf activity led boyars to pay monster hunters well, opening an Adventure in Varushka for its units. Varushkan congregations received the Free Folk donations, though Karsk lost its earlier bonus.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Hahnmark lost the extra liao and Synod votes it had gained from an earlier judgement as a side effect of the Free Folk mandate.

t.Brocéliande: Navarr with herb gardens in Brocéliande could improve them for one wain less weirwood than normal until the Summer Solstice 385YE.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fleets were offered the option to support the Osseini spy network in Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark lost the additional liao and votes granted by an earlier judgement.
t.Hercynia: Great Forest Orcs began settling in Hercynia, and Navarr herb gardens there could be improved at reduced weirwood cost.
t.Holberg: Sand Fisher orcs provided two random herbs to each farm in Holberg every downtime.
t.Karsk: Congregations in Karsk lost the additional liao and votes granted by an earlier judgement.
t.Liathaven: Thunderous Tread of the Trees sent possessed plants against armies, fortifications and the few remaining steadings in Liathaven, with loss of life expected and the Jotun bearing the brunt.
t.Madruga: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast in Madruga to contain the desiccating blight on the Great Grasses.
t.Miaren: Great Forest Orcs began settling in Miaren, and Navarr herb gardens there could be improved at reduced weirwood cost.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt lost the additional liao and votes granted by an earlier judgement.
t.Tassato: Congregations in Tassato lost the additional liao and votes granted by an earlier judgement.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar lost the additional liao and votes granted by an earlier judgement.
t.Therunin: Navarr with herb gardens in Therunin could improve them for one wain less weirwood thanks to Great Forest Orc expertise.

385YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: The Brass Coast's Sails of the First Flame cast the Hallow of the Green World, flooding the Empire with Spring magic, blooms and boggarts, while Lord Rain aided farmers and healers. The Senate's appraisals covered Kahraman's broken roads and Bastion's challenge of Timoj. Grendel envoys were expected at Anvil to discuss extending the peace treaty. Varushka completed Kostjyas Respite and the Iron Roads, and Zenith's Crucible of Fate was finished. Other entries covered the Whisper Gallery, a blight in Madruga, Suranni wizards, the vyig and Metri, and Mournwold orcs seeking to join the Marches. The Civil Service also corrected rumours about storm deaths and Thule slavery, and the outcomes of Winter Sentinel Gate conjunctions were reported.

n.Dawn: Dawnish heroes saw the traitor Renee du Loire captured in the Barrens and executed, Dawn may share in the trade of Kostjyas Respite, and Summer patronage of the Eastern Sky was among the magical matters raised.
n.Druj: Imperial raiders destroyed the Sleepless Nightmare and the scorched liege in the Barrens, though Garsnag Mudchurner, Varag Soulflayer and Serra Grubfeast survived, and the Synod debated what the Empire should ultimately do with the Druj.
n.Grendel: Salt Lord delegations were expected at Anvil to negotiate a possible extension of the two-year peace treaty, as Grendel merchants sought to trade on the uncertainty, while the port of Oran stayed closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly passed three mandates, one granting new powers to support other nations, while Highborn generals helped rebuild Zenith and backed the liberation of the Barrens; meanwhile Bastion faced the appraised challenge of Timoj.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Ethengraw Armoury and Illarawm Ossuary neared completion, quietening Stonecliff Brakkalo's criticism, and the Illarawm offered meditative techniques to help orcs ignore the voices of angry ancestors.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces were driven back in Sermersuaq, Jarl Roneth was defeated and Lasambrian raiders were beaten in Kahraman and Kallavesa, but they reinforced Skallahn, raised a fane in Greenwall, threatened Oddmire and continued fortifying Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly welcomed Great Forest Orcs to settle in Miaren and Hercynia, prepared for vallorn stirrings caused by the Spring enchantment and reclaimed many bandits in Therunin, while Imperial heroes recovered the Tairiscint na Foraoise in Brocéliande.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn magicians unleashed the Hallow of the Green World, an appraisal proposed ways to restore Kahraman's sabotaged roads and bridges, and a creeping ash blight was found in Madruga's Great Grasses.
n.The League: A new sword academy in Holberg drew Urizen sword scholars and some controversy, the Empire moved to drive the vyig from Temeschwar and Hag Queen servants from Metri, and a hidden chamber was discovered beneath the Mint in Tassato.
n.The Marches: Most former Mournwold thralls asked to become Marchers but would not give up their belief in reincarnation; meanwhile Faraden harbourmasters at Caitun offered trade to the Marches, and Jotun threatened Oddmire from Bregasland.
n.Thule: The Civil Service confirmed that the Thule truly had freed their slaves, though Otkodov remained a harsh authoritarian society struggling with food shortages.
n.Urizen: The Crucible of Fate was completed in Zenith to restore hope there, though Urizen scorned further help from Highguard, its sword scholars were invited to Holberg, and its priests still would not welcome the Free Folk.
n.Varushka: Varushka completed Kostjyas Respite and the Iron Roads, linking nearly every major settlement, but awakening monsters threatened the Semmerlak ports and the Lord of the Broken Barrow offered friendship to its people.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark confronted the people of Sermersuaq who had accepted boons from Blood-on-the-Snow, saw Jotun pushed back in Stark and Tanikipari, and gained a possible trade opening with the Faraden at Caitun.

t.Bastion: An appraisal considered how Bastion and the Bay of Catazar territories might rise to the challenge of Timoj, starting with a competition and ending in a vast commission.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the territories of the Bay of Catazar were named in the appraisal on rising to the challenge of Timoj.
t.Bregasland: Imperial heroes delivered supplies to the Scraggy Bole and rescued Tall George from the Jotun, but the chance to rouse Old Marjoram was not taken and the Jotun there threatened Oddmire.
t.Brocéliande: Imperial heroes recovered the Tairiscint na Foraoise at Kay's Lament and rescued injured Marchers at the Silent Copse.
t.Hercynia: Great Forest Orcs began settling near its weirwood groves, and a slight upsurge in vallorn activity caused by the Spring enchantment was contained by well-prepared Navarr.
t.Holberg: The new Holberg Scholars of the Sword Academy invited Urizen sword scholars to teach, drawing interest, opposition and worries about one of Holberg's infamous sons.
t.Kahraman: An appraisal set out how its Jotun-sabotaged roads and bridges might be restored, and Imperial heroes drove off Lasambrian jotun threatening wagon trains in Serra Briante.
t.Kallavesa: Imperial heroes dealt with Lasambrian jotun in Skymark and protected a group of hylje.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the recent troubles in Karsk were cited as the scale the Therunin bandit problem will no longer reach.
t.Liathaven: The regio at Broker's Wynd was used to unleash devastating Spring magic on the Jotun, though work continued on their fortification there.
t.Madruga: A strange blight of ash and dust was growing at the heart of the Great Grasses, contained but not removed by Spring magic despite the Silver Chalice's investigation.
t.Miaren: Great Forest Orcs were welcomed by the Navarr Assembly to establish steadings near the weirwood groves.
t.Mitwold: Oddmire was left under threat from the Jotun in Bregasland after the conjunction to rouse Old Marjoram went untaken.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos anger at Imperial involvement in the failure of their joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon damaged trade.
t.Mournwold: Most of its former thrall orcs asked to become Marchers while others left for Jotun lands, a Summer enchantment fell over the territory, and missions in Southmoor failed to rescue Wise Maggie or stop Little Robin.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Grendel questioners had visited the tomb of Emperor Barabbas there on their way to Anvil.
t.Ossium: The completion of Kostjyas Respite helped resolve one of the lingering challenges for the people of Ossium.
t.Otkodov: Its former orc slaves were confirmed as free citizens, though Otkodov remained highly stratified and was suffering food problems from the change.
t.Sea of Snow: A flotilla of more than seventy fleets partly mapped the Sea of Snow and reached the Faraden coast, with monster-hunting opportunities also reported there.
t.Sermersuaq: The Shuttered Lantern, priests and the Silent Bell moved against those who accepted Blood-on-the-Snow's boons, while Imperial heroes drove back Jotun scouts and defeated Jarl Roneth.
t.Skallahn: With the conjunction there not taken, the Jotun reinforced their borders and established a fane in Greenwall.
t.Spiral: Salt Lord Kaliact of Spiral, whose earlier offer of a separate agreement the Senate rejected, might send representatives with the Grendel delegation.
t.Tassato: An incongruous wall beneath the Imperial Mint suggested a hidden chamber, reachable by nine people through a Sentinel Gate conjunction before rising waters reflood it.
t.Temeschwar: The Empire set out to drive the vyig from Temeschwar once more, and the Rod and Shield led efforts against Hag Queen servants in Metri.
t.The Barrens: Imperial heroes destroyed the Sleepless Nightmare and the scorched liege and executed a captured traitor, but several Druj leaders escaped, the Rahvin remained enslaved, and Highborn generals pursued liberation rather than conquest.
t.The Semmerlak: Kostjyas Respite opened on its northern shore, but an awakening sovereign took a particular interest in the Semmerlak ports.
t.Therunin: The Spring enchantment caused a slight, contained vallorn upsurge, and Navarr guides brought many East Ashes bandits back to the Great Dance.
t.Zenith: The Crucible of Fate was completed at the Spire Calator, Highborn generals helped rebuild, and Imperial heroes had mixed results against tormented spirits and miasma pillars.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Supplies were successfully delivered to the Scraggy Bole at the Orchard of Tom Wiscall.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Tall George, an apprentice of Mott, was rescued at the Dry Marsh and the Jotun stymied.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Injured Marchers were rescued at the Silent Copse and the threat addressed.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: The Tairiscint na Foraoise was recovered at Kay's Lament.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market was listed among those concerned in the fight against the vyig.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Most of the Lasambrian jotun waiting to ambush wagon trains on Isabella's Track were defeated or driven off.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: Lasambrian jotun on the Cold Path of Kaisa were dealt with before they could slaughter a group of hylje.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Oddmire was left under threat from the Jotun in Bregasland.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Wise Maggie was not rescued at Tollerton Green, and the traitor Little Robin escaped at Friar Tommy's Grave despite the Jotun being engaged.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Mentioned in passing: the Merchant-boyar of the Bittershore was listed among those concerned with events around the Semmerlak.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Many Jotun scouts were defeated at Vahne's Field and the Jotun driven back.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Jarl Roneth was defeated at Siward's Folly and the sword recovered for Barien.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: The Jotun established a fane in Greenwall after the conjunction to stop it went untaken.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named directly; the page refers only to Spiral as a whole through Salt Lord Kaliact.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: The haunting presence in the forests around the Fortress of Salt proved to be Hag Queen servants, and Imperial magicians led by the Rod and Shield set out to drive them back to Winter.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: The Sleepless Nightmare was destroyed at the Broken Glade along with most of its Druj escort.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The scorched liege and most of the Burnt Fist coven were destroyed at Berena's Tree, but Garsnag Mudchurner fled his holt.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Varag Soulflayer and the tormented spirits at Soulflayer's Refuge survived the Imperial attempt to kill him.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: A rise in bandit activity was largely defused as Navarr guides and brands persuaded many bandit steadings to come home, though some outlaws remain.
r.Zenith/Iteri: A gate anomaly left the tortured souls at the Spire of the Everlasting Dusk unrested, and the outnumbered heroes retreated in good order.
r.Zenith/Lustri: A miasma pillar at the Spire of Twisting Shadow was destroyed, but its guardians remained because of a gate anomaly.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The tormented spirits at the Ring of Solace ruins were laid to rest with minimal harm to the heroes.

385YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The Jotun took Fort Braydon, dominated Braydon's Jasse and pressed into the Jade Range. Imperial forces freed the Dour Fens, so Bregasland is Imperial again, though Ottermire and Gravenmarch remain in Jotun hands. In the Barrens, eleven Imperial armies defeated eleven Druj armies, drove them from Bitter Strand, Saltmarsh and the Plains of Teeth and took the Spires of Dusk. Tens of thousands died, and the Hounds of Glory were lost. The Granite Pillar cleared two more miasma pillars in Zenith. Spy networks were dismantled in Skallahn and disrupted in Feroz. The page listed three battle opportunities, Jotun and Druj threats in Liathaven, Sarangrave and Sermersuaq, and many conjunctions.

n.Dawn: Dawnish forces shared the costly Barrens victory, in which the knights and yeofolk of the Hounds of Glory made the ultimate sacrifice taking the Spires of Dusk. Dawnish armies suffer a three-tenths penalty to territory conquered in the Barrens, and Dawnish titles were tasked with laying dead knights to rest and slaying a herald of Agramant in Semmerholm.
n.Druj: The Druj lost a clash of eleven armies a side and were driven from Bitter Strand, Saltmarsh and the Plains of Teeth, losing the Spires of Dusk. The Thornwasp clan nonetheless plotted to ambush thorns crossing the Feverwater, and Serra Grubfeast's forces at Dawnguard were named as a battle target.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel were thought likely to be behind an attack on Shantarim and other islands in Feroz, but there were no definitive reports.
n.Highguard: Highborn armies can no longer issue the Crusading Storm order but may generate mandates for their assembly while on campaign. They gain bonuses when attacking into Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow, and Highguard had a force weight of 18 for the battles.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs were listed with a force weight of 5 for the coming battles.
n.Jotun: The Jotun conquered Fort Braydon in Kahraman but lost the Dour Fens of Bregasland, keeping only Ottermire and Gravenmarch there. The Jarl of Kierheim dismantled the Imperial spy network in Skallahn, Jarl Iduna hunted Navarri in Liathaven, and a herald-backed force marched on the Pride of Ikka's Tears.
n.Navarr: Navarri trapped behind Jotun lines in Liathaven faced slaughter by Jarl Iduna's warband. In Therunin, Eira Larksong's Assembly judgement succeeded in helping former bandits, while Druj threatened Mudlark's Haven. Navarr had a force weight of 50.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast lands in Kahraman suffered the Jotun invasion and lost Braydon's Jasse, and the Jade Range was nearly taken too. A conjunction in Madruga sought to destroy the Dry Patricians.
n.The League: League titles were tasked with recovering Misericorde's Blade and killing the Vyig in Holberg, and with clearing out heralds in Metri in Temeschwar. The League had a force weight of 17.
n.The Marches: Marcher-held Bregasland was liberated from Mathilda Fisher, with the Strong Reeds leading the fight and a battle opportunity offered to end her threat. Marcher armies gain extra strength in Upwold, Mitwold and Mournwold, and the Strong Reeds gain it in Bregasland.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Pride of Ikka's Tears was described as lying near the borders of the Jotun, the Thule and Tsirku.
n.Urizen: The Granite Pillar, aided by Senate-paid mercenaries, cleared two more miasma pillars in Zenith. The Citadel Guard will begin to deteriorate again after the Summer Solstice, and the Court of the White Fountain cannot fall below 1,000 strength.
n.Varushka: Varushkan armies avoid the general Barrens penalty, but they generate fewer victory points when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies. Varushka had a force weight of 11.
n.Wintermark: A Jotun force accompanied by heralds of Hayaak marched on the Pride of Ikka's Tears in Sermersuaq and threatened five wains of mithril, and Custodian Tuija Dunning was responsible for stopping it. Wintermark had the largest force weight, at 58.

t.Bregasland: Imperial forces freed the Dour Fens and restored the territory to the Empire, though Ottermire and Gravenmarch remain Jotun-held. A battle opportunity offered the chance to end Mathilda Fisher's threat.
t.Feroz: Reports told of an attack on Shantarim and several islands, affecting the naval operations spy network there. The culprit was unclear, though the Grendel were suspected.
t.Holberg: Two conjunctions targeted Holberg: recovering Misericorde's Blade at Elsbeth's Well and killing the Vyig at Drusilla's Farm.
t.Kahraman: The Jotun invaded from Liathaven, conquered Fort Braydon and nearly took the Jade Range. Only armies stationed in the Cinnabar Hills prevented a wider loss, and a battle opportunity offered to investigate a gathering of champions.
t.Liathaven: Jarl Iduna's warband hunted Navarri still in the territory and threatened to uncover the Imperial spy network. The Imperial Spymaster, Bernard Dugdale, was responsible for stopping her.
t.Madruga: A Saturday conjunction to the Dry Patch in the Great Grasses aimed to destroy the Dry Patricians, under the Grandmaster of the Silver Chalice.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army may billet here, and Marcher armies fighting here gain extra strength.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Highborn and Urizen armies attacking into Zenith from Morrow, or defending Morrow, gain bonuses.
t.Mournwold: A conjunction to the Overton Ruins in Greensward offered the chance to lay ghosts to rest. Marcher armies fighting here gain extra strength.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Court of the White Fountain here cannot be reduced below 1,000 military strength.
t.Sarangrave: Thornwasp Druj, accompanied by heralds of Arhallogen, prepared to ambush thorns arriving in Bloodwater Marsh, in a fight under Druj miasma.
t.Semmerholm: A conjunction to Axmure aimed to slay the Amaranthine Devourer, a herald of Agramant. The Adamant Gate cannot fall below 1,000 strength.
t.Sermersuaq: A Jotun force marched on the Pride of Ikka's Tears and threatened five wains of mithril. Further conjunctions targeted a relic at Stark and Theodric Irontongue in the Suaq Wastes.
t.Skallahn: The Jarl of Kierheim dismantled the Imperial spy network and rooted out its scouts. A newly built fane of Estavus in Greenwall equipped Jotun warriors.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle was named as responsible for a conjunction to recover the Gyre's Edge in the Barrens.
t.Temeschwar: A conjunction to Agnieszka's Grove in Metri aimed to clear out heralds, under the Grandmaster of the Rod and Shield.
t.The Barrens: Eleven Imperial armies defeated eleven Druj armies, liberating Bitter Strand, Saltmarsh and the Plains of Teeth and taking the Spires of Dusk at a terrible cost. Many conjunctions and a battle for Dawnguard followed.
t.Therunin: Guides and citizens successfully helped former bandits back into the Great Dance after a Navarr Assembly judgement. Druj scouting threatened future attacks on Mudlark's Haven.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: the Pride of Ikka's Tears lies near the border with Tsirku.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army may billet here, and Marcher armies fighting here gain extra strength.
t.Zenith: The Granite Pillar and Senate-paid mercenaries cleared two more miasma pillars, and the struggle against the fear was reportedly going well.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch remains in Jotun hands despite the liberation of the wider territory.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: A conjunction to the Greywater Estates sought to force the Jotun to retreat, under the General of the Strong Reeds.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Ottermire remains in Jotun hands despite the liberation of the wider territory.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: only through the title of the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market, who was made responsible for a conjunction in Utterlund.
r.Holberg/The Morass: A conjunction to Drusilla's Farm aimed to kill the Vyig, under Irada von Temeschwar.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: A conjunction to Elsbeth's Well aimed to recover Misericorde's Blade.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Jotun conquered Fort Braydon and now dominate the region, and a battle opportunity offered to discover more about a gathering of champions.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Jotun were well on the way to conquering the region. Conjunctions aimed to stop the Jotun on the Path of the Liscano family and to slay Venator, a herald of Hayaak, on the Sylvan Track.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Ring: A Friday conjunction to the Shattered Glade aimed to rescue the trapped Navarri and kill Jarl Iduna.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: A conjunction to the Overton Ruins, where combat was unlikely, aimed to lay ghosts to rest under the Friar of Honour's Rest.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: A conjunction to Ormthak's Path aimed to kill the Thornwasp ambushers and their heralds of Arhallogen amid the Druj miasma.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: A conjunction to Melusine's Field aimed to slay the Amaranthine Devourer, a herald of Agramant.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: A conjunction to Nestori's Lament aimed to recover a relic from the Ender of Virtue.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Conjunctions to Ymma's Howe and Ardith's Rest aimed to stop the Jotun advance on the mithril mine and to kill Theodric Irontongue.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: A recently constructed fane of Estavus here had equipped the Jotun force marching into Sermersuaq, for unknown reasons.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: A conjunction to Agnieszka's Grove aimed to clear out heralds.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Druj were driven out, and a conjunction to Spinner's Retreat aimed to slay Venomclaw, a herald of Arhallogen.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: A Sunday battle opportunity aimed to break the forces of Serra Grubfeast and claim Dawnguard.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The Druj were driven out. Conjunctions aimed to recover the relic of Adelmar, recover a stockpile, and meet the Vendarri on Greenstone Isle.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: A conjunction to the Blooming Grove aimed to kill tepel Zortog Ashtouch.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: A conjunction to Jagged Stream aimed to drive off the Druj.

A long December.d: Snowstorm Henk will still complete Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti's research into the orcs who guarded Emperor Ahraz's tomb. A skeleton crew will keep aiding the Great Library of Hacynian, delaying its vallorn investigation to Summer 386YE while allowing one research commission per season. The Department can now support only one of three titles: the Minister of Historical Research, the Advisor on the Vallorn or the Imperial Advisor for the Feni. An administrative motion will decide which, or none. Gerard La Salle proposed auctioning the right to direct research through the Bourse. Ris Steelfist's patron-funded plan replaces the Senate's 22-throne bodyguard payment, and military units can now take on the War of Whispers adventure.

n.Highguard: Highguard's scholars are helping to speed the vallorn research, and wealthy Highborn chapters are among the patrons funding heroes to protect scholars from the Whisper Gallery.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Archivist remarks that one of his scholars would quickly be caught by the Jotun if he became a war scout.
n.Navarr: The Department will still give skeleton support to assembling the Navarr archives at the Great Library of Hacynian, but the vallorn investigation will now finish at the Summer Solstice 386YE. The Whisper Gallery's agents tried to set fire to the library.
n.The League: The League's support is helping the vallorn research. The Lepidean University was targeted by Whisper Gallery arsonists, and League scholarship faces the same threat that the new protection fund is meant to counter.
n.Urizen: Urizen spires are among the patrons funding heroes to protect scholars. Octavia of Stream's Source Spire now leads one of the Department's three research teams.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: information recovered from Brocéliande is helping to shorten the vallorn research for the Great Library.
t.Holberg: The opportunity that came with consecrating the Walls of Holberg led the Senate to retrain Department researchers as prognosticators, which helped leave the Department short of scholars.

A murder of one.d: Three kinds of Spring boggart appeared: crow-like Corbs that unmake crafted things, Greenteeth that lure rescuers to stagnant water and kill them, and Grimmelkint that feed on forests and curse anyone who harms them. Unless they are dealt with, every forest faces a two-rank production penalty. Professor Beatrice of Holberg suggested herding those heading for Anvil back through the Hall of Worlds portal. Arhallogen proposed a Navarr Synod mandate urging merciless war on the Jotun; Corey Wayfarer and Nathair Autumngale offered competing alternatives. High Priestess Shivaarn asked the Conclave to lift Siakha's enmity, promising only a half-dozen observing heralds and no attack on the Conclave for two seasons.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen's open patronage of the Druj orcs is cited as what makes the eternal a problematic ally.
n.Grendel: Three rough Grendel orcs from the Temple of Tempest Jade carried High Priestess Shivaarn's offer on Siakha's behalf, hinting at the imminent shattering of the Grendel treaty. Shivaarn may care more for her goddess than for the Salt Lords' concerns.
n.Jotun: Arhallogen wants the Navarr to stop sparing Jotun lives. If the mandate passes, Navarr armies would inflict 10% more casualties on the orcs of Narkyst, Kalsea and Lasambria for a year, and the slaughter would be plain to every force in the territory.
n.Navarr: The Navarr assembly could enact Arhallogen's mandate, gaining 10% more casualties against the Jotun at the cost of 20% fewer victory points and earning an arcane projection from the eternal. Alternatively it could take Corey Wayfarer's version without the projection, or Nathair Autumngale's rejection, which would keep thorns to balanced attack or solid defence.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Segura is named among the places whose forests the Grimmelkint are swarming, and a Freeborn corsair's boastful letters drew Siakha's attention.
n.The League: Greenteeth caused unpleasant incidents in Holberg, and Professor Beatrice of Holberg proposed herding the Grimmelkint back through the Hall of Worlds portal. She also speculated that they might one day coexist with forest owners.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen marks one edge of the Grimmelkint swarms descending on Imperial forests.
n.Varushka: Small groups of Greenteeth were sighted in Ossium, and Varushkan forests fall within the Grimmelkint swarms' reach. The tale's Varushkan heroine, Sasha, fights the beasts in Inga Tarn's name.
n.Wintermark: Greenteeth struck in Kallavesa, and Sermersuaq's forests face Grimmelkint swarms. Wintermark's 381YE mandate urging honourable war against the Jotun is what Arhallogen scorns.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Temple of Tempest Jade that sent Siakha's message lies on the far side of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Holberg: Greenteeth lurking in stagnant water caused unpleasant incidents here, and Holberg's Professor Beatrice led the study of the boggarts.
t.Kallavesa: Greenteeth ambushed travellers in Kallavesa's marshes by mimicking cries for help, as in the tale of Ulf Unmelten and Sasha, and there were real incidents here.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Ulf jokes that monsters belong in Karov, not Kallavesa.
t.Ossium: Small groups of Greenteeth were sighted in Ossium.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura is named as one extent of the Grimmelkint swarms threatening Imperial forests.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is named as one extent of the Grimmelkint swarms threatening Imperial forests.

Anyone but you.d: Directed by the Assembly of Nine, the Silent Bell helped magistrates arrest and execute most of the cult ringleaders, but Kaarina White-Eye, Maarik the Golden Tongue and Wemba the Bloody fled with their followers. Under a Wintermark Assembly mandate, backed by the Loyalty Assembly, priests and Stormcrows saved nearly half of those who took Agramant's bargains; more than two score confessed, were fined and became Frayed, possible recruits for Wintermark's new army. Theodric Irontongue's unrepentant Walkers of the Wastes are now Averil Olsen's responsibility. The Shuttered Lantern recovered boons, vis and texts, found the Bleeding Ice, a Heart's Blood source the Conclave must endow or see destroyed, and tracked the herald Ender of Virtue.

n.Dawn: Tyburn of House De Rondell, the Dawnish Grandmaster of the Shuttered Lantern, will receive the boons recovered from the cultists and is responsible for intercepting Ender of Virtue in Stark.
n.Jotun: The escaped cult leaders are all driven by hatred of the Jotun and vow bloody vengeance on them, with Kaarina White-Eye believed to have fled west towards the Jotun border; a maimed Jotun orc, Harla, testified against Theodric Irontongue.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Cardinal of Vigilance, Gaelen Embercast of Navarr, raised the Assembly of Nine motion that sent the Silent Bell to Sermersuaq.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Maarik the Golden Tongue grew wealthy mediating trade deals with the Thule in the Silver Peaks, where she is now believed to be hiding.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: two recovered ritual texts would be recognisable to any Urizen who had studied the ceremonies of the Black Drop Society.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's priests and Stormcrows saved many of the Sermersuaq Winterfolk who bargained with Agramant, leaving a body of Frayed warriors and others who could form the core of the nation's new army. Three Winterfolk cult leaders remain at large and Averil Olsen must deal with Theodric Irontongue's cult.

t.Kallavesa: The herald Ender of Virtue is heading for the Kallavesa border carrying something from the Winter realm believed capable of blighting the Kallavesi herb gardens.
t.Sermersuaq: The territory was purged of most of Agramant's cultists through executions and clemency, though three ringleaders fled, the Walkers of the Wastes remain unrepentant and the Bleeding Ice awaits the Conclave's decision.

r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: Mentioned in passing: Maarik the Golden Tongue was a Suaq mediator from the north of the East Floes before her hall was burned and she turned to Agramant.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Maarik the Golden Tongue and her followers are believed to be hiding in the Silver Peaks, sheltered by several allies.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Ender of Virtue and its cultists were tracked in Stark heading towards Kallavesa, with an opportunity to confront them at Nestori's Lament.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Theodric Irontongue is preaching to the Walkers of the Wastes, who will remain a threat here unless stopped, with an opportunity to strike at them at Ardith's Rest.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The Bleeding Ice, a boulder near the Hot Springs weeping four pawns of winter vis each season and linked to Wemba the Bloody, was found here, and the Conclave must endow it or see it destroyed.

Blood will thicken.d: Commissioned by the Senator for Necropolis, the appraisal found that pilgrims lacked a reason to come, not the means. Eilian proposed that artists submit designs to the Assembly of Nine at the Summer Solstice. Pharos' Water offered the Dragonbone Symbol Wayfarers Guide to the winner if the Senate builds the design. The full commission would need 1000 wains of white granite, 250 Thrones and three years, and would make Bastion the undisputed centre of the Way. National assemblies could pass mandates committing citizens' granite and coin, at the cost of supporting other causes. Highguard could give 25 wains and 50 crowns each season. Alternative League and Varushkan mandates, and an Urizen refusal, were also proposed.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly could pass a mandate pledging its citizens' spare resources, worth 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns a season for a year. Doing so would stop Dawn backing other causes through mandates during that time.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Urizen's proposed refusal calls for the repatriation of Grendel-held Spiral.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly could redirect the nation's building zeal to the holy city, giving 25 wains of white granite and 50 crowns each season until it is complete. This would sacrifice its earlier mandate's benefits and any other financial mandates, and abandoning the work later would deeply wound Highborn Pride and Ambition.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs could mandate support for the holy city, contributing 4 wains of white granite and 8 crowns a season for a year. That would block other financial mandates for the nation during that time.
n.Navarr: The appraisal was carried out by the Navarr historian Eilian Sweetwater, chosen for his insight into travellers. Navarr could also pledge 12 wains and 24 crowns a season by mandate.
n.The Brass Coast: The Senate's separate appraisal into restoring Kahraman's infrastructure went to Naomi. The Brass Coast could pledge 8 wains of white granite and 16 crowns a season to the holy city by mandate.
n.The League: The League could pledge 20 wains and 40 crowns a season by mandate. Rafael Barossa d'Apulian proposed an alternative mandate appealing to League Pride to outdo the other nations.
n.The Marches: The Marches could pass a mandate giving 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns a season for a year towards the holy city.
n.Urizen: Urizen could pledge 12 wains and 24 crowns a season by mandate. Aspar instead proposed a refusal that would bar any Urizen aid to Bastion and prioritise rebuilding Zenith and repatriating Spiral.
n.Varushka: Varushka could pledge 20 wains and 40 crowns a season by mandate. Vasilmir Radovanovna Esskivic proposed a Vigilance-themed alternative to pave the holy city with Varushkan stone and line it with wards.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark could pass a mandate contributing 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns a season for a year towards the holy city.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Castle of Thorns is cited as a grand fortification that, unlike the proposed holy city, exists for defence rather than faith.
t.Bastion: The White City of Bastion, birthplace of the Way, is the only place the Grand Inspiration of the Way could be built. If completed, it would become the indisputable centre of the Way and draw pilgrims from across the known world.
t.Bay of Catazar: Completing the holy city would bring a vast influx of foreign pilgrims to the Bay of Catazar, fulfilling the aim of raising its territories to the challenge of Timoj.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Walls of Holberg are cited as a grand defensive work, unlike a monument dedicated purely to faith.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Senate also commissioned Naomi of Virtue's Rest to appraise how Kahraman's infrastructure might be restored.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Necropolis raised the motion that commissioned the pilgrim appraisal.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Aspar's proposed Urizen mandate names the repatriation of Spiral as a priority above funding Bastion.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Bloody Great Theatre is cited as a site that draws visitors from across Temeschwar and the Empire but is too small to attract foreign pilgrims.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Aspar's proposed Urizen mandate would put the rebuilding of Zenith ahead of any support for the holy city.

Butterfly in reverse.d: High Lord Mukhali Tchemetzi offered to supply 60 wains of white granite and Faraden builders if the Empire provided 15 wains of weirwood and 45 crowns for transport. Once complete, any Imperial fleet could trade at Caitun for orichalcum, weltsilver, green iron and blood whelks, with Wintermark and Marcher fleets profiting most. Winterfolk, Marcher and Freeborn fleets could also hunt Sea of Snow monsters for oil, whale horn or kraken's ink. Separate proposals, which the page does not record as enacted, would dredge the Westmere near Meade, raising taxes and opening mithril trade with the Tseriyn and ilium trade with the rival Salagiin, provided dredging finished before Spring 386YE.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the shipwrecked sailors in the story fear being caught on the Jotun side of the Faraden border, and note that the Jotun shun the sea there.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn fleets, swift enough to base themselves at Caitun, gained the chance to hunt the monsters of the Sea of Snow once the port opened after the Autumn Equinox 385YE.
n.The Marches: Marcher fleets would earn a bonus to their production trading at Caitun and could hunt Sea of Snow monsters. Dredging the Westmere at Meade was also proposed, which would create a possible Alder of Meade buying Tseriyn mithril in exchange for Marcher farm produce.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly and shares only in the general opportunity for Imperial fleets to trade at Caitun.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk fleets would gain a production bonus trading at Caitun and could hunt Sea of Snow monsters. Dredging the Westmere was proposed to benefit Fisk, with a possible Mediator of Fisk buying Salagiin ilium for coin and beggar's lye.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the sailor Hoepel regrets swapping the shark-filled Bay of Catazar for the Sea of Snow.
t.Bregasland: The proposed dredging of the Westmere would raise taxation from Bregasland by 2 thrones each season, though the page does not record the dredging as carried out.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's port of Fisk stood to gain from the proposed Westmere dredging, which would add 2 thrones of tax each season, and from a possible ilium-buying Mediator of Fisk based there.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Meade's docks are compared unfavourably with major Imperial ports such as Cargo, Siroc and Atalaya.
t.Mitwold: Dredging the Westmere near Meade was proposed as a ministry commission costing 50 weirwood, 30 white granite and 20 thrones, which would raise Mitwold's taxation by 5 thrones each season and enable a mithril trade.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page and is linked only through the wider Imperial opportunity at Caitun.
t.Sea of Snow: The flotilla's voyage reached the Faraden coast, and with Caitun opened to Imperial ships, fleets could now hunt the seahemoths, cambion-whales and kraken that haunt these waters.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, which instead discusses Kallavesa's port of Fisk and its prospects if the Westmere were dredged.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: The proposed dredging of the Westmere would give Meade March the coastal quality, potentially allowing a future shipyard at Meade and easing passage for ships trading with Caitun.

Chasing you home.d: In Kahraman, the Jotun had taken Fort Braydon, helped by large elite warbands. Three of these warbands sent their banners to Morogvejo, where the ghodi Alok Surefoot would cast runes and issue orders. The Empire could intercept those orders, seize the banners, and kill Alok to take the Spear of Bounty. If he kept it, Hayaak's heralds would inflict 250 casualties a season on Imperial armies in Kahraman. In Bregasland, the defeated Mathilda Fisher was gathering her followers at Rock Foot Wood to retreat to Hordalant. The Empire could have her executed by a Marcher to prevent her becoming a martyr, and could deal with the Loyalty priest Bushel Sykes.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish enchanters are given as an example of how a captured Spear of Bounty might be offered to a Summer court in return for patronage of the Eastern Sky.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that Alok Surefoot regards the Navarr as no better than human Druj.
n.Jotun: The Jotun had taken Fort Braydon in Kahraman and were gathering warband banners and orders at Morogvejo under the ghodi Alok Surefoot. Meanwhile their allies in Bregasland were retreating towards Hordalant, which left them exposed to an Imperial strike at either site.
n.Navarr: Alok Surefoot hates the Navarr, so any Navarr armies in Kahraman would be the first target of Hayaak's heralds if the Spear of Bounty was not taken from him.
n.The Brass Coast: Fort Braydon, a long-standing Freeborn stronghold in Kahraman, had fallen to the Jotun. The Morogvejo opportunity offered a chance to blunt the Jotun warbands operating there.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the ruined Morogvejo watchtower once kept watch over Tassato.
n.The Marches: The rebellion in Bregasland was near collapse, and only a proper execution of Mathilda Fisher by a Marcher would kill the dream of Free Bregas. Dealing with Bushel Sykes would let the Marcher Assembly root out remaining traitors.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Alok Surefoot's earlier boon from Hayaak sent heralds to slaughter many of the Thule Dragon's prized warlocks in Sermersuaq.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: vengeful Summer heralds summoned by Alok Surefoot had earlier stalked the tundra of Sermersuaq.

t.Bregasland: Imperial forces had liberated much of the territory, and Mathilda Fisher was preparing to flee from Graven Rock. Her execution by a Marcher would end Free Bregas, while her escape or an unceremonious death risked future unrest.
t.Hordalant: Hordalant was the intended refuge of Mathilda Fisher and her followers, some of whom were levies from its fens. If she escaped, the Fishers would withdraw there and resurface later.
t.Kahraman: The Jotun held Fort Braydon and were gathering warband banners at Morogvejo. Imperial armies in the territory faced 250 casualties a season from Hayaak's heralds unless Alok Surefoot lost the Spear of Bounty.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the old Morogvejo watchtower once kept watch over Madruga.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Morogvejo watchtower once overlooked it, and recent unrest in the Mournwold is cited as a warning about rebellion taking root in the Marches.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Alok's earlier boon from Hayaak saw heralds hunt and slaughter Thule warlocks on its tundra.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the ruined watchtower on Morogvejo hill once kept watch over Tassato.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: listed among the regions Imperial forces had liberated from the Jotun.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Imperial forces had made gains into Ottermire, the home of the rebel priest Bushel Sykes.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: Mentioned in passing: listed among the regions liberated by Imperial forces.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Fort Braydon had fallen and the Jotun banners now flew from its walls. The Kahraman strike opportunity, against the warbands and Alok Surefoot gathered at Morogvejo, was set out under this region's heading.

Children in bloom.d: The enchantment touched only territories that were Imperial at the end of Winter 384YE. Strange blooms spread everywhere, briars felt invigorated, and herds, harvests and perhaps births all increased. For a season, farms and forests could be diversified for free, and citizens could exchange their resources for farms. The trods surged with power, and Navarr Spring magicians with mana sites could harvest vis. Chaos fruit from Brocéliande could be cultivated in forests until the end of the Spring Equinox, prompting Navarr calls for vigilance and possible Navarr and Highborn mandates. A resonance of ruin badly damaged the Blood Red Roads and Sunset Roads. The civil service would spend 26 Thrones a season maintaining them unless the Senate instructed otherwise.

n.Dawn: Magical blooms were in great demand ahead of the Dawnish Festival of the Net. Astolat and Semmerholm stood to lose Blood Red Roads income if maintenance stopped.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens, which the Druj held, was excluded from the enchantment's benefits.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Spiral and Feroz, held by the Grendel, were excluded from the enchantment's benefits.
n.Highguard: Highguard's new White Roads suffered only minor erosion. The Highborn assembly had the opportunity to raise a mandate, with the grey pilgrims searching out chaos fruit forests.
n.Imperial Orcs: Swelling herds boded well for the Shepherd of the Great Herd and for the orcs raising their own herds in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland and Liathaven, which the Jotun held, were excluded from the enchantment, and the winter fighting with the Jotun in Liathaven is recalled.
n.Navarr: The trods, newly extended by the Voice of the Quiet Forest, surged with power, and Navarr Spring magicians with mana sites each gained vis. Enfys Larksong urged openness about chaos fruit cultivation, and a Navarr mandate to track it was proposed.
n.The Brass Coast: The Sails of the First Flame cast the enchantment, but the Sunset roads in Segura and Madruga were damaged by the resulting Spring magic.
n.The League: A fashion for wearing unique flowers swept the League. The late La Volpe's Blood Red Roads, which enrich Temeschwar, Sarvos, Tassato and Holberg, bore the brunt of the ruinous damage.
n.The Marches: The blooms added grandeur to Marcher spring festivals. Marcher farms could build landskeeper menhirs without the usual diversification cost, and Upwold's road income depended on maintenance.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: new Navarr trods in Sküld, in Thule-held Otkodov, are noted as part of the enlarged network.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the magical blooms were in demand ahead of the Urizen Night of Flowers.
n.Varushka: The newly completed Iron Roads were untouched, which Varushkan builders attributed to their protections. Karov's Blood Red Roads benefits were still at risk.
n.Wintermark: Growing herds boded well for Winterfolk returning to Sermersuaq and for the proposed Hunt of the North. The Pilgrim's Trail in Kallavesa weathered the season through hard work.

t.Astolat: Astolat's farms and businesses risked losing their Blood Red Roads income, and its vallorn-plant farms would be listed if both Navarr and Highborn mandates passed.
t.Bastion: The White Roads linking Bastion sustained less damage than other roads, though they showed some erosion in wilder places.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: as a Jotun-held territory, Bregasland's resources gained none of the enchantment's benefits.
t.Brocéliande: Excluded from the enchantment, Brocéliande was the source of the chaos fruit, and there were concerns that cultivating the fruit near its vallorn could be dangerous.
t.Casinea: Casinea's Blood Red Roads income was at risk, and its vallorn-plant farms would be listed if both mandates were enacted.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: as a Grendel-held territory, Feroz was excluded from the enchantment's benefits.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark's extra farm and business income from the Blood Red Roads would erode unless the roads were maintained.
t.Hercynia: Concerns were raised that cultivating chaos fruit in Hercynia could be dangerous because of the vallorn there.
t.Holberg: Holberg's Blood Red Roads income was threatened by the damage, and the city's streets bloomed with lilac.
t.Kallavesa: The Pilgrim's Trail was less affected than other roads, though its mystics and priests had a challenging season keeping the paths clear of marsh growth.
t.Karov: Karov benefits from the Blood Red Roads, which stop short of Delev, and that income was at risk if maintenance lapsed.
t.Liathaven: Jotun-held Liathaven was excluded from the enchantment. Its newly restored trods joined the Navarr network, and cultivating chaos fruit there was seen as dangerous.
t.Madruga: Madruga's Sunset roads were damaged by the Spring magic, and its Blood Red Roads income depended on Senate-funded maintenance.
t.Miaren: Miaren's Blood Red Roads income would slowly erode if the roads were not maintained.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the war in Mitwold is used as an example of where a Bregasland briar might have spent the season.
t.Necropolis: The White Roads connecting Necropolis held up better than most, showing only minor erosion.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: new trods in Ossium are noted as part of the enlarged Navarr network.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: new trods in Sküld, within Otkodov, are noted as part of the enlarged Navarr network.
t.Reikos: The granite White Roads serving Reikos suffered only light erosion.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's Blood Red Roads income was at risk, and its fashionable citizens led the craze for wearing spring flowers.
t.Segura: Segura's Sunset Roads were badly worn by the Spring magic, and their benefits would fade unless the Senate allowed maintenance to continue.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's Blood Red Roads income was at risk, and its vallorn-plant farms would be listed if both mandates were enacted.
t.Sermersuaq: The surge in herds boded well for the Winterfolk returning to Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Imperial Orcs raising herds in Skarsind could expect them to grow significantly.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: as a Grendel-held territory, Spiral was excluded from the enchantment's benefits.
t.Tassato: Tassato's Blood Red Roads income would decline by a Throne a season if maintenance stopped.
t.Temeschwar: The Blood Red Roads built by Temeschwar's late La Volpe bore the brunt of the damage, putting the territory's road income at risk.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held Barrens was excluded from the enchantment, and recent fighting there had left some soldiers disillusioned.
t.Therunin: Concerns were raised that cultivating chaos fruit in Therunin could be dangerous because of the vallorn there.
t.Upwold: Upwold's Blood Red Roads income would slowly erode unless the roads were maintained.

r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Mentioned in passing: in the story, the briar Amwell and his comrade Bruna recall having fought at Rebeshof.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: Sküld's new trods are part of the Navarr network through which the Spring magic surged.

Colourblind.d: Investigation found the blight was a Winter curse from the Wasteland, spread by the Parched or Ashwalkers and sustained by a handful of powerful Dry Patricians, members of the Aldea di Tutamen who sought physical immortality. Dry Patricians can be destroyed only by Words of Ending at magnitude 18. Ashwalkers can be dispersed with Turns the Circle, though some are slowly becoming Dry Patricians. Exorcism and Insight fail against them. Heralds of Ossegrahn supplied pure Spring water that lures the creatures. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered the Silver Chalice's Grandmaster a chance to destroy some. Regrow the Land's Heart only holds the blight in check, and its origin remained unexplained.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Aldea di Tutamen traced their roots to the exodus from Highguard, and their robes recalled pre-Highguard patricians.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr members of the Silver Chalice drew unsettling parallels between the blight and the vallorn, while stressing it was not an equivalent threat.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn hakima and kohan died investigating the blight on their own lands. The Sails of the First Flame coven's Regrow the Land's Heart and Hallow of the Green World kept it from worsening. The source was a Freeborn family, the Aldea di Tutamen, cursed into Dry Patricians.
n.The League: League magicians and archers fought alongside the effort. A Holberg doctor who came with Lord Rain's heralds declared that the Parched were a sickness that must be fought.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni sentinels appear guarding the edge of the blight, and a Urizen stargazer suggested the desiccated land might be an extrusion of the Winter realm.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a League doctor from Holberg, Doctor von Holberg, rescues a hakima in the story and joins the effort alongside Lord Rain's heralds.
t.Madruga: The Great Grasses in Madruga were being consumed by a Winter blight that only ritual magic was holding back. Failure to destroy the Dry Patricians would mean the Grasses could never be restored and would need constant magical containment.

r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Sentinel Gate was to open on the edge of the blight deep in the Great Grasses. There, heroes could lure out and fight the Dry Patricians, though the battleground would likely be destroyed even in victory.

Construct Anvil Library Scriptorium.d: Using the Second Imperial Wayleave, Claus Friedrich von Holberg announced a sinecure costing 12 wains of white granite and three thrones in labour, taking three months to build. The Scriptorium will provide liao and votes in the Imperial Synod. It and the sodality of the Anvil Library will be governed by the Armarius of the Anvil Library, an Imperial title appointed and revoked by the Wisdom Assembly, with tenure until death, resignation or revocation. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the three thrones and twelve wains of white granite after the Spring Equinox 385YE. Once complete, the Wisdom Assembly may appoint the Armarius.

n.The League: The League gains a new Imperial sinecure in one of its cities, Rodez in Sarvos, whose holder will control liao and Synod votes tied to the Anvil Library.

t.Sarvos: The Anvil Library Scriptorium is to be built in Sarvos, funded after the Spring Equinox by Giacomo Corvinoscuro's donation of money and white granite.

r.Sarvos/Foracci: The Scriptorium is to be constructed in Rodez in Foracci, taking three months to complete before the Armarius can be appointed.

Construct Garden of Glory.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Astolat, the motion used an opportunity from the Long Walk Home wind of fortune (Spring 382YE) to build at reduced cost: 8 wains of weirwood and 2 thrones in labour, with three months to construct. The sinecure produces 6 liao and carries no Synod votes. Eadric Fjellrevening de Rondell Rezia di Tassato provided the weirwood and money after the Spring Equinox. Once completed, the Keeper of the Garden is appointed and revoked by the Navarr National Assembly.

n.Navarr: The Navarr National Assembly gains the power to appoint and revoke the Keeper of the Garden, a new liao-producing sinecure, once the garden is completed.

t.Therunin: The Garden of Glory is to be raised in Therunin, taking three months to build and yielding 6 liao for its keeper.

Construct Hall of the Hunters.d: Announced in Spring 385YE under the Legion Engineer's authority, the Hall of the Hunters is a sinecure arising from the Watching my mistakes wind of fortune. It required 12 wains of white granite, 3 thrones in labour and three months to build, plus standard costs. Liv Tidgaring provided the 3 thrones and 12 wains of white granite after the Spring Equinox. Once complete, the Wintermark National Assembly may appoint the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq by judgement. The hall will also open a new adventure, Hunt the Suaq Wastes, to military units from Dawn and Wintermark.

n.Dawn: Dawn's military units will gain access to the new Hunt the Suaq Wastes adventure once the hall is complete.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark National Assembly will gain the right to appoint the Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, and Wintermark military units can take part in the Hunt the Suaq Wastes adventure; Liv Tidgaring supplied the granite and labour costs.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq, held by Wintermark, is to gain the Hall of the Hunters at Lake Atkonaroq, a new sinecure tied to hunting in its wastes.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The hall is to stand at Lake Atkonaroq in the Suaq Wastes, which become the setting for the new Hunt the Suaq Wastes adventure.

Construct Hall of the Seven.d: Announced by Bertrand, Bearer of the First Imperial Wayleave, the commission followed the wind of fortune "The bones of what you believe". It cost 10 wains of weirwood, 10 wains of mithril and 5 thrones in labour, and took three months to build. The mithril was given in memory of Amaan Embercast, and weirwood and coin came from many Navarr donors, including Corwyn Heartsbane, Nathair Autumngale and several of the Eternal and Nighthaven lines. Corwyn added a further 6 wains of weirwood after the Summer Solstice. Once the hall was finished, the Spear of the Seven became available for annual election by the Navarr senators, and could be revoked by the National or Imperial Synod. The hall also opened an adventure for Navarr military units exploring the ruins of Terunael.

n.Navarr: Navarr gained a new national position, the Spear of the Seven, elected each year by its senators. Its military units also gained the chance to explore the ruins of Terunael.

t.Miaren: The Hall of the Seven was built in Navarr-held Miaren and became the seat of the new Spear of the Seven.

Construct House of Healing.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Reikos, the motion aimed to give Imperial heroes access to much-needed magical items and to make Therunin the "Heart of Healing" in the Empire, with the responsibilities required by Ossegrahn. Construction cost 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, and took three months. Many individuals donated money after the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice, and Raewynn Farkas provided the weirwood in two deliveries of 10 wains. Once the House of Healing was complete, the position of Hand of the Healers became available for the Imperial Conclave to appoint through a Declaration of Candidacy.

n.Navarr: The motion was proposed by the senator for Navarr-held Therunin, and many of the donors who paid for the work bore Navarr names, giving the nation a new ministry on its land.

t.Therunin: The House of Healing was built in Therunin, and its backers hoped the ministry would make the territory the Heart of Healing in the Empire, bound by the responsibilities Ossegrahn required.

Construct Kragg's Hollow.d: Kragg's Hollow was a mana sinecure built in Skarsind at a cost of 10 wains of mithril, plus 20 crowns in labour and three months of construction. The announcement said it was funded with the prosperity of Ashborn Kragg, with thanks to the Imperial Spymaster. After the Spring Equinox 385YE, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad provided the 10 wains of mithril and Kostjya provided 2 thrones 4 crowns. Once construction was completed, the new title of Scholar of Kragg's Hollow became available for appointment by the Imperial Conclave using a Declaration of Candidacy.

n.Imperial Orcs: The new mana sinecure was raised in Skarsind, a territory the Imperial Orcs held at the time, adding a Conclave-appointed magical title within their lands.

t.Skarsind: Kragg's Hollow was built in Skarsind as a mana sinecure, and the territory became the seat of the new Imperial title Scholar of Kragg's Hollow.

Construct Lowther's Lift.d: Proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Kallavesa, the motion commissioned the self-funded folly. The motion text gave the cost as 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns, but the costs were set by the Wind of Fortune: 15 wains of weirwood, 20 crowns in labour and six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, William Lowther provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of weirwood, but Jotun raiders took 5 wains of weirwood. Fern provided another 5 wains after the Summer Solstice. Following the actions of Yanya Uranduln, the lifts needed another five wains of weirwood and three more months. Once completed, the lift will give the Custodian of the Singing Caves a ministry to buy mithril at set prices.

n.Jotun: Jotun raiders took 5 wains of weirwood meant for the lift after the Spring Equinox, which delayed and added to the cost of the project.
n.The Marches: The senator for Mitwold proposed the project in Mournwold, and Marcher-held land stands to gain new mithril supplies through the Custodian of the Singing Caves.

t.Mournwold: The lift was being built in the Singing Caves near Overton, and once finished it will open new mithril veins there and create a ministry for the Custodian of the Singing Caves.

Construct Palace of Flowers.d: The Senator for Skarsind proposed the motion and the Senator for Morrow seconded it. It passed. The Palace of Flowers is a garden for the Yerende sept, costing 60 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns in labour, and taking six months to build. After the Spring Equinox, Irontide Flax, Bloodcrow Rasp, Abel the Rounder of Sarangrave Reforged, Redhand Gezzar and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov donated money and weirwood towards it. Once it is finished, the Yerende will join the Imperial Orcs and share their herbal lore. The key part of that lore is a set of realmsroot potion recipes useful to orc magicians.

n.Imperial Orcs: Once the folly is finished, the Yerende sept will join the Imperial Orcs. They will bring herbal lore, including realmsroot potion recipes useful to orc magicians.

t.Skarsind: The Senator for Skarsind proposed the motion, which places the new Palace of Flowers in the territory. It will be ceded to the Yerende sept once built.

r.Skarsind/Solvihill: Solvihill is the site of the Palace of Flowers, a garden folly due to take six months to build for the Yerende sept.

Construct Runeforge in Hahnmark.d: The motion authorised construction of a runeforge in Hahnmark at a cost of 45 wains of weirwood, 30 wains of white granite and 30 wains of mithril, with a year needed to build it. Materials arrived in instalments through 385YE. Derowen supplied the largest share: all 30 wains of white granite, 24 wains of mithril and 44 wains of weirwood. Lumi Warmthbringer, Æthwin Aldwynson, Kaapo Kingfishering, Arsenio Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato and Erasmo di Tassato provided smaller contributions. Once finished, the new post of Keeper of the Runegrott was to be filled for the first time by a Tally of the Votes among the military unit captains of Wintermark at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a runeforge in its own territory, and the captains of its military units were given the right to choose the first Keeper of the Runegrott by Tally of the Votes.

t.Hahnmark: The runeforge was built in Hahnmark under a motion proposed by Hahnmark's own senator, and it was completed using materials supplied by several donors over 385YE.

Construct Smokehouse of Atalaq.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion commissioned a vast smokehouse in Atalaq with a network of supporting structures across Sermersuaq, as set out in the Write the lines wind of fortune. It was framed as aiding Sermersuaq's recovery from Jotun invasion and restoring pride to the people of the ice. The project cost 40 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour on top of the motion's cost, and took three months to build. Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason provided the weirwood and labour after the Spring Equinox. Once complete, it would share 60 crowns among Sermersuaq's farms and grant qualities to the fourth Wintermark army.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the motion cites Sermersuaq's recovery from Jotun invasion as one reason for the great work.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a great work that gives its prospective fourth army qualities drawn from Suaq traditions. The Sermersuaq and Hahnmark senators backed it, and a Wintermark citizen, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, supplied its weirwood and labour costs.

t.Sermersuaq: Atalaq becomes the site of a vast smokehouse, with supporting structures across the territory. Once complete, it will share 60 crowns among Sermersuaq's farms as the territory recovers from Jotun invasion.

Construct Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchan.d: The motion created a ministry in Hanuri, Temeschwar, costing 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of mithril and 5 thrones in labour, and taking three months to build. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided all the materials and labour costs after the Spring Equinox. The ministry is overseen by the Keeper of the Tome, appointed by tally of the votes of the League's business owners. The motion intended the post to carry tenure, but a position appointed by tally of votes cannot do so, so the Speaker for the Senate was to raise an administrative motion making it a one-year post. With construction complete, the first appointment was expected at the Summer Solstice 385YE, provided that motion passed.

n.The League: The League gained a new ministry in Temeschwar, funded by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, with its Keeper of the Tome chosen by the votes of League business owners from the Summer Solstice 385YE.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule's territory of Otkodov appears in the ministry's name, but the page says nothing further about Thule's involvement.

t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named in the title of the Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, but nothing is built or decided there.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar became the site of the Temeschwar Otkodov Mana Exchange, a new ministry overseen by a Keeper of the Tome.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri is where the Mana Exchange was built, a three-month construction completed using white granite, mithril and labour paid for by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar.

Construct the Great Chain of Sarvos.d: Sagua i'Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, announced the project as the Steel Rings of Sarvos, using the Chain against Chains opportunity, with Merchant Prince Shauni di Vergo, Senator of Sarvos, gathering funds. It would also help Sarvos build and protect a navy if the Naval Arsenal were built. The cost was 130 wains of white granite, 260 crowns in labour, 10 thrones upkeep and a year's construction. Contributions of money and granite came from many donors between Spring and Autumn 385YE. At the Summer Solstice the Senate amended the name to the Great Chain of Sarvos.
