Once complete it has strength 3,000, rising to 6,000 against shore offensives aimed at capturing Cigno.

n.The League: League citizens, led by the Master of the Koboldi, the Senator of Sarvos and the merchant princes of Sarvos, organised and largely funded a defence against naval attack on one of their cities.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos was to gain a fortification of strength 3,000 guarding against naval attack, which could also help it build and protect a navy if the Naval Arsenal were built.

r.Sarvos/Cigno: Once complete, the Great Chain's strength doubles to 6,000 against any shore offensive aimed at capturing Cigno.

Cost.d: Eleven armies and thirty thousand champions, aided by Summer and Winter warriors, fought nearly a dozen Mallum armies, the twisted Black Wind and the Rivers Run Red curse. A slave uprising aided by the Winter Sun won the Bitter Strand, though the freed slaves held the Fangs mithril mine and barred the Empire. At the Shadowmere a Druj ambush on the Citadel Guard became a victory, taking the Saltmarsh, and the Vendarri sued for terms. The Hounds of Glory pressed on, rallied the faltering Empire at the Battle of Dusk and broke into the citadel, but the army was destroyed. Over fifteen thousand Druj fell. Five Sentinel Gate conjunctions followed.

n.Dawn: All four Dawnish armies led the campaign, and the Hounds of Glory sacrificed themselves to seize the Spires of Dusk, leaving rows of Dawnish dead and the Black Wind singling out Dawnish soldiers for slaughter.
n.Druj: The Druj lost the Bitter Strand, Saltmarsh, Plains of Teeth and the Spires of Dusk, and more than fifteen thousand Mallum orcs, though they still hold the forests and remain defeated but not beaten.
n.Highguard: The Seventh Wave scouted, foiled Druj traps and brokered the Vendarri surrender, which is now under discussion with the Highborn over the fate of Saltmarsh, while Highborn soldiers were among the thousand who fell at the Shadowmere.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun came from Ossium to free Druj slaves, smuggled weapons to the slaves of the Fangs to spark the uprising and helped win over the Vendarri, while the Bronzehoard reavers found a Druj stockpile now offered as a conjunction.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: respectable Navarr bands fought with the Hounds of Glory, and Navarr on the campaign recognised echoes of the Holt of the Oak in the weirwood of the Spires of Dusk.
n.The League: The Wolves of War and Towerjacks fought in the campaign, the Wolves locked in an inconclusive skirmishing duel with the Hunting Scorpion, and League bands swelled the Hounds of Glory.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard turned the Druj ambush at the Shadowmere into victory and, protected by Winter magic, lost not a single sentinel or magician throughout the whole campaign.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle and Golden Axe fought alongside Summer schlacta through the campaign, with Varushkan dead among the thousand lost at the Shadowmere, and the Bargainer of the Iron Tower is offered a conjunction to secure abandoned mithril.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark bands fought with the Hounds of Glory and Winterfolk advised comrades on crossing the flooded Saltmarsh.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is named as one of the homes to which the Dawnish dead may be brought back for burial.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the new Spires of Dusk are compared in scale to the Silent Sentinel in Casinea.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks arrived fresh from a triumphal procession through Holberg, and Raguk Chainforger's wealth is likened to that of Holberg's merchant princes.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Druj het Ortgut Spirebreaker is named for toppling spires in Morrow and Zenith.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun came south having driven the Druj from Ossium, and the broken Tower of the Scorpion there is dwarfed by the Spires of Dusk.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: veterans recalled lessons learned at Exile in Reikos, the Spires were compared to its citadel, and a few cases of the Reikos flux broke out in the Saltmarsh.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Druj tepel Zortog Ashtouch is withdrawing to coordinate with the ghulai of the Salt Flats of Sanath, carrying a list of regios, and the Polemarch of Highwatch is asked to intercept it and disrupt their schemes.
t.Semmerholm: A Druj force is escorting the Agramant herald the Amaranthine Devourer through Semmerholm towards the Pits of Brychel, and the Knight-protector of Winter is charged with killing it; Semmerholm is also a home for the Dawnish dead.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Bronzehoard reavers went into the Barrens seeking goods to sell to the orcs of Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: light infantry from Tassato served with the Wolves of War in their skirmishes against the Hunting Scorpion.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the walls of the Spires of Dusk are said to echo those of Temeschwar.
t.The Barrens: The Empire now holds five regions of the Barrens including the Spires of Dusk, though the Druj still control the territory and its forests, the Fangs are held by independent orc rebels and the Rivers Run Red curse still blights its waters.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Navarr saw echoes of the Holt of the Oak in Therunin in the weirwood construction of the Spires of Dusk.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater is named as one of the homes to which the Dawnish dead may be brought back for burial.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard marched south from a freed if not healed Zenith, and Ortgut Spirebreaker is named for toppling spires there.

r.Reikos/Broken Ride: Mentioned in passing: Broken Ride itself is not named; Reikos appears only through references to the citadel of Exile and the Reikos flux.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: A small White Lion force has entered Axmure escorting the Amaranthine Devourer towards the Pits of Brychel, and the Sentinel Gate opens to Melusine's Fields so the Knight-protector of Winter can stop them.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Bitter Strand fell to the Empire after a bloody battle and an uprising of the Fangs' slaves, who now hold the mithril mine and refuse the Empire access, and a conjunction to Spinner's Retreat targets Venomclaw and the heralds of Arhallogen.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: Mentioned in passing: Farweald is listed among the forests the Druj twist with magic against Imperial pursuers.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The flooded, blighted Saltmarsh was taken after the Battle of the Shadowmere and the Vendarri sued for surrender, while a conjunction to the Steadfast Pines offers a chance to loot Raguk Chainforger's stockpile.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Druj regrouped in the warded Bleaks to strike at the Battle of Dusk and have fallen back there, and the Sentinel Gate opens to the Blooming Grove for a strike on Zortog Ashtouch.

Daylight fading.d: Mine and forest owners in Miekarova, Karov and Volodmartz now share 35 ingots and 35 forest measures, and Ossium's forest owners share 70. The Crow Roads in Karsk were reduced to the same level. Five Bourse resources each gain 2 wains a season. Ossium is no longer under-populated, so Varushka could support a fourth army, and the Assembly may offer guidance. Tasya urged the Malinov to release the axe Hunger. Boyar Svetlana refused and offered yearly axes for Varushkan generals instead. The Charnel Lord offered spy networks into Thule and Druj lands, while a rival mandate would reject him. Further mandates could encourage bargaining with sovereigns or peaceful contact with orcs.

n.Druj: The Charnel Lord offered to help Varushkans set up a spy network in the Forest of Ulnak, promising the Druj would not notice it unless someone acted foolishly. This is an offer that depends on a Synod mandate.
n.Highguard: Jared proposed a Partners of Greatness mandate in which Highguard would support Varushkan efforts to deal with the orcs in their lands. It would fail automatically if the Varushkans do not enact their own mandate.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named, though the Thule holdings in Crow's Ridge in Skarsind would be covered by the proposed Urdur spy network.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a previous Varushkan claimant to be Alderei reborn reportedly destroyed the Jotun meeting stone, antagonising the western orcs.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the inspiration of Ratibor of Temeschwar and his attributed saying, 'if you can destroy it, you control it', circulated among Varushkans eyeing the Senate-held Bourse resources.
n.Thule: The Charnel Lord offered to help Varushka spy on Sküld and Urdur, and on Thule holdings in Varushka, Sermersuaq and Skarsind, unseen by Hinodir of the Bright Orb. A rival mandate warned this could break the peace treaty. A further mandate could encourage peaceful dealings with the Thule in Varushka.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen pilgrims visiting the Maze of Zoria recalled Clytemnestra's threat to destroy the Citadel Guard, feeding Varushkan talk about reclaiming Bourse resources.
n.Varushka: The completed Iron Roads enriched Varushka's mines, forests and Bourse resources and made a fourth army possible. The National Assembly now faces choices on the new army, the axe Hunger, the Charnel Lord's spy offer, and whether to bargain with sovereigns or orcs.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the jealousy of Wintermark still rankles with Varushkans, and the hylje of Wintermark were contrasted with the monstrous creatures of Varushka.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The Empire knows almost nothing of the Forest of Ulnak. The Charnel Lord offered to help Varushkans establish a one-season spy network there, reached through the twisted woods of Branoc.
t.Karov: With the Iron Roads open, Karov's mine owners share 35 ingots and its forest owners share 35 forest measures each season.
t.Karsk: The Crow Roads' extra benefit fell to match the Iron Roads at 35 ingots and 35 measures. Tasya of the Black Feathers visited the Malinov and Karsk's priests, volhov and wise ones on the Charnel Lord's behalf.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's mine and forest owners each gain a share of 35 ingots and 35 forest measures now that the Iron Roads are complete.
t.Ossium: The Iron Roads brought settlers and trade, so Ossium is no longer under-populated, which lets Varushka support a fourth army. Its forest owners share 70 forest materials, and its former Druj septs are among the orcs Varushkans might treat with.
t.Otkodov: The Charnel Lord offered to guide Varushkan scouts unseen through the mountains into Otkodov to spy on Sküld and Urdur, claiming the Thule dragons would not discover them.
t.Sermersuaq: If created, the proposed Urdur spy network would also report on Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks of Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: If created, the proposed Urdur spy network would also report on Thule holdings in Crow's Ridge in Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Ratibor of Temeschwar is cited as an inspiration for Varushkan talk of reclaiming Bourse resources.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: work was completed on Kostjyas Respite, the new Varushkan port-town on the northern shores of the Semmerlak.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: the Empire already has a map of Verthandi, unlike the rest of Otkodov.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's mine and forest owners share 35 ingots and 35 forest measures each season thanks to the Iron Roads.

r.Karsk/Branoc: The Charnel Lord sleeps beneath the Broken Barrow here. Captains using his spy network must leave a blood gift at the barrow, and woods-wise guides from Branoc's vales, human and independent orc, would lead them.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule-controlled Krevsaty would be covered by the proposed Sküld spy network, and its orcs are among those Varushkans might be urged to contact peacefully.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: Tasya urged the Malinov of Moresvah to return the bloodthirsty axe Hunger to the Iron Helms. Boyar Svetlana refused, offering yearly axes for Varushka's generals if the Assembly endorses keeping Hunger hidden.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: The Thule holdings in Miechernya would be covered by the proposed Urdur spy network, and its Thule orcs might be approached for peaceful deals.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: The new port at Bittershore helped clear away the last of Ossium's economic problems.
r.Ossium/Bonewood: The Thule-controlled Bonewood would be covered by the proposed Sküld spy network, and its orcs are among those Varushkans might contact.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Echofell would be covered by the proposed Sküld spy network.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: The sept of the Menrothat in Nearweald is named among the orcs Varushkans could be urged to make peaceful contact with.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Mentioned in passing: the Webwood is listed among the Varushkan lands controlled by the Thule.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: The Empire knows little of Sküld. The Charnel Lord offered a Varushkan-only spy network there, which would also report on Krevsaty, the Bonewood and Echofell.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: The Charnel Lord offered a Varushkan-only spy network in Urdur, which would also report on Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks, Crow's Ridge and Miechernya.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Thule holdings in the Silver Peaks would be reported on by the proposed Urdur spy network.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Thule holdings in Crow's Ridge would be reported on by the proposed Urdur spy network.

Drinking song for the socially anxious.d: Axou narcotics sellers Evander Slak and Hippolata of Kaban planned to trade outside the Forge, including more doses of Bone Dust. A Jarmish dhow, nominally commissioned by a Sarcophan merchant, docked at Spirewood Wharf in Elos offering rare spices to Urizen's finest magicians, reachable through a Sentinel Gate conjunction. A herald of Ephisis brought an Autumn trading game to the Hall of Worlds. Thule's Five Fang Consortium headed south from Otkodov seeking investment. The would-be sodality The Rising Tide sought to meet Heilyn Bronwen's Rest. The herald Venator sought to speak with Cecilia de Gauvain, and Apulian orcs, led by Merchant Prince Mahiri Kaliact, prepared to seek League citizenship.

n.Dawn: The herald Venator, who once hunted the yeofolk of House Perigord, now sought to speak peacefully with Cecilia de Gauvain in the Hall of Worlds, needing an Imperial citizen to invite him in.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Merchant Prince Mahiri Kaliact di Apulian is described as formerly the Salt Lord of Spiral.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, but the roads of its territory Casinea were busy with merchants heading for Anvil.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, though Venator was last seen in the Jade Range of its territory Kahraman, terrorising Dawnish yeofolk.
n.The League: A contingent of Apulian orcs was to camp with the League, with Mahiri Kaliact intending to swear an oath to the League's egregore and become the first of her people to take citizenship, while others sought to discuss bishops, fashion and the Test of Citizenship.
n.Thule: The Five Fang Consortium, Thule business folk, artisans and Autumn magicians with limited prospects under warlock rule, headed to Anvil seeking Imperial investment for ventures in their homeland after the end of slavery in Otkodov.
n.Urizen: A Jarmish ship moored at Spirewood Wharf in Elos sought well-placed Urizeni magicians to buy rare spices, with the Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks responsible for overseeing an expedition through the Sentinel Gate; the trade was framed to sidestep the Jarmish embargo since the seller was a Sarcophan merchant.

t.Casinea: Casinea's roads were busy with merchants, traders and peddlers from across the Empire and beyond, all bound for the summit at Anvil.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Venator was last seen in Kahraman's Jade Range terrorising Dawnish yeofolk.
t.Otkodov: The end of slavery in Otkodov was slowly bringing change, giving rise to the Five Fang Consortium, some reportedly former slaves, who sought outside capital for projects there.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Mahiri Kaliact di Apulian, who sought League citizenship, was formerly the Salt Lord of Spiral.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Mentioned in passing: the Jade Range is where Venator was last seen hunting the yeofolk of House Perigord.

Everything is broken.d: Dawnish scouts contacted Houses Robar and Garland, who asked for weapons, armour and mithril. Prognosticators advised patience, but the Hounds' sacrifice sparked a rising, and contact with the rebels was lost as the Druj counter-attacked. On the Sunday of the summit the Empire could strike Dharrik Bonebite's force at Merigionne. Killing enough of it would let the rebels take Dawnguard and give the Empire the Barrens. Other objectives were to kill Bonebite, save the captive Rousers of Glory from sacrifice to Agramant, and cast The Basalt Citadel with Sorin's boon. Senators could move early to assign the territory, a choice with risks either way.

n.Dawn: Dawn mourned and celebrated the Hounds of Glory, and its Assembly was urged to propose a fitting memorial rather than re-raise the army. Its kin in the Barrens rose in revolt, and the Dawnish there would be furious if the territory went to any other nation.
n.Druj: Reeling from the loss of the Spires of Dusk, the Druj under Serra Grubfeast sent Dharrik Bonebite to crush the Dawnish rebels and sacrifice captive troubadours for Agramant's aid. Plaguetouch sent another force to slaughter the Rahvin at the Fangs, while holdouts raised slain Imperial soldiers to spread terror.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; its only link is the Castellan of Spiral Castle, who was tasked with recovering Gyre's Edge.

t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the yeofolk of Ville Deleroi in Semmerholm asked the Dean of Laroc Cathedral to lay their extinct house's knights to rest at Bloodrun Dell.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Castellan of Spiral Castle, Maryc, was made responsible for recovering House de Casillon's ancestral blade, Gyre's Edge.
t.The Barrens: Dawnish houses and yeofolk across the Barrens rose against the Druj. A victory at Merigionne would let the rebels seize Dawnguard and bring the territory under Imperial control, ready for the Senate to assign.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Mentioned in passing: Bitter Strand is listed among the regions the Empire had taken from the Druj.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The Druj gathered their forces and counter-attacked the Dawnish rebels in Murderdale as well as Dawnguard, cutting off all contact with them.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Now taken from the Druj, Saltmarsh was the destination of a conjunction to Hadrienne's Lament, where the Champion of Ambition was to recover the Goblet of Adelmar from the undead remains of Hadrienne de Deveou's retinue.

Expand Academy of Arms.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Madruga, the commission followed the Build up my body Wind of Fortune. It cost 25 wains of white granite, 50 crowns in labour and three months to build. The new title, Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine, grants 10 liao, 20 Synod votes and one free upgrade of a basic military unit each season. Materials and money came from several citizens, many of them of the Lighthouse-That-Was and the Astral Observatory, including Laelius Webworker, Spyridonakes, Limonos and others. With construction complete, the Assembly of Ambition would make the first appointment at the Summer Solstice 385YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen's Redoubt gained an expanded Academy of Arms, largely funded with white granite and coin from Urizeni citizens of the Lighthouse-That-Was and the Astral Observatory, and a new Synod title tied to military training.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt's senator proposed the expansion of the Academy of Arms within the territory, and it was built there to house the new Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine.

r.Redoubt/Siluri: The Academy of Arms in Siluri was expanded, creating Adelmar's Shrine, whose prelate can upgrade a basic military unit for free each season.

Fade out again.d: Irada von Temeschwar and Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti carried mandates to root out the Vyig. Once fear of reprisal broke, accusations flushed them out across the League, and Varushka barred its doors against them. The purge cost Sorensdromen, Travy Mudrosti and Drusilla's Obelus, all destroyed, and the Vereski Stzena were slaughtered in retaliation. Confiscated businesses in Temeschwar, Holberg and Karsk await new owners. Fleeing Vyig joined Druj forces, opening conjunctions at Elsbeth's Well and Drusilla's Farm. In Metri the Rod and Shield ended the haunting. The Grand Enchantrix and her Spites remain, however, with a conjunction to Agnieszka's Grove offering the chance to finish them.

n.Druj: Raids revealed that the Vyig had long smuggled bite into the Empire from Druj lands. Druj forces now protect fleeing Vyig in Utterlund and the Barrens, and Druj valuables are said to have been seized.
n.The League: The League drove the Vyig from its cities through dawn raids and street battles, though Valentin von Temeschwar's call for mercy was ignored. Confiscated Vyig businesses in Temeschwar and Holberg are now available to new owners.
n.Thule: Thule trade through Metri was never disrupted, because the northern orcs propitiate the Mirror of Spite whenever her servants appear. They had assumed the creatures were part of a Temeschwari deal with the Thrice-cursed Court.
n.Varushka: Following Velko Perunovich Razoradze's mandate, Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti ensured every Varushkan door was barred to the Vyig, leaving them nowhere to flee. Travy Mudrosti was razed, and confiscated Vyig holdings in Karsk passed to Vaclav.

t.Holberg: A bar brawl in Holberg became a week-long street battle between bravo gangs, and the Sorensdromen forest, used as a bite dead-drop, burned down. A Holberg herb garden was razed, a rank three business was confiscated, and citizens may request new businesses here without the usual two-crown fee.
t.Karsk: A herb garden in Karsk was razed by the Vyig to hide its contents. A rank three forest and a rank three herb garden, both formerly Vyig-owned, were confiscated and their deeds given to Vaclav Mladenovich Kosti.
t.Temeschwar: Two running battles against the Vyig were fought through Temeschwar's streets. Rank four and rank two businesses were confiscated and given to Irada von Temeschwar, and new businesses may be requested here without the two-crown fee.
t.The Barrens: The Vyig had been smuggling bite out of the Barrens. Druj who crossed the border there now escort fleeing Vyig through the territory towards the port of Leen.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Vyig thieves stole Misericorde's Blade, a Sand Fisher symbol of resistance against the Druj. The Sand Fishers asked Merchant Prince Jonah Yakovitch to recover it and promised to pay well.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Drusilla's Obelus, used by the Vyig to smuggle bite since its creation, was burned to the ground. A conjunction to Drusilla's Farm was assigned to Irada von Temeschwar to deal with the Vyig and their Druj escort.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The Sand Fisher scout Grey Tooth tracked the Vyig thieves to Elsbeth's Well, where they met orcs of the Mallum. A conjunction opens there to recover the stolen blade.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: The Rod and Shield slaughtered the Hag Queen's beasts, ending the haunting and the disruption to trade. The Grand Enchantrix and her Spites remain, and Grandmaster Sakari Nightscale is responsible for a conjunction to Agnieszka's Grove to deal with them.

Grind.d: Five Jotun armies led by King Gudmunder Arasonn's Fist of Ulven attacked from Liaven's Glen, accompanied by Summer knights and seemingly every major Jotun champion's warband, among them Stephen of Sarcombe's Mournwold traitors and the mountain-banner of Geht Ahan. The Red Wind Corsairs, Black Thorns and Quiet Step chose to strike and withdraw, giving ground. Fort Braydon's exhausted garrison could not hold; Gudmunder reportedly shattered its weirwood gate, and defenders who did not surrender were killed. The Jotun took Nestor's Bounty, offered captives servitude or death, and dug in short of full control of Jade Range. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Kahraman, apparently linked to the Jotun champions, was identified for the Spring Equinox.

n.Jotun: Five armies of Narkyst under King Gudmunder Arasonn, with the Hierro and a host of champions, captured Fort Braydon and Braydon's Jasse and now hold eight-tenths of Jade Range, digging in with armed camps rather than chasing Navarr ambushes.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns and Quiet Step harried and ambushed the Jotun while giving ground, but the orcs showed them no mercy, dumping Navarr dead in unmarked mass graves or burning them on pyres.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost Fort Braydon, with much of its garrison trapped and killed or forced to surrender, while the Red Wind Corsairs rescued what residents they could as the Jade Range families fled, fought, or faced servitude.
n.The Marches: Stephen of Sarcombe and the treacherous scions of the Mournwold fought at the forefront for the Jotun in Braydon's Jasse, though his earlier destruction ironically kept the Jotun from easily assaulting Serra Briante.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Ice Fishers of Ldansk were last seen conquering Sermersuaq, and Jotun champions came south swollen by victories in the north, offering the same Choice given there.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman's northern lands were overrun as Fort Braydon fell, Braydon's Jasse was conquered and most of Jade Range taken, with Serra Briante and Serra Damata now exposed to further attack.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun-held forest served as the springboard for the invasion, with forty thousand orcs marching south out of it into Kahraman.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's Mournwold traitors fought for the Jotun and kept close to the borders of the Mourn.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Ice Fishers were last seen in its conquest, and the Choice offered on Jade Range is the same harsh one given there.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Skjaldirborn's general invoked the memory of Skallahn as he rallied his warriors.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The whole Jasse fell to the Jotun after Fort Braydon was stormed and its weirwood gate shattered, leaving the fortress in orc hands and garrisoned by the Fist of Ulven.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: War returned only six months after the last fighting, Nestor's Bounty fell, and eight-tenths of the region came under Jotun control as its proud families fled or fought rather than take the Choice.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Jotun-allied mountain folk raided its mines, and while Stephen's destruction blocked an assault this season, the Jotun are now free to strike at its mithril.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Geht Ahan's mountain warband harried caravans out of Damata, though the Jotun cannot attack it in the same season as Serra Briante with the same force.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: The five Jotun armies struck south out of Liaven's Glen to begin the assault on Braydon's Jasse.

Have you seen me lately.d: Sung agreed to a Friday-night parley with the Archmage of Night, asking for the Shaman of Wintermark and up to four others to discuss three mysteries, with no petitions. Ylenrith, still an enemy of the Empire, sought to regain trust and warned of a 'Cold Sun'. Rhianos would discuss Atun's Ring, the sword Fortinbras and the Eastern Sky, but refused looting requests. Ephisis auctioned slots for City of Gold and Lead heralds and waived parley protections. Kaela offered tribute to her Grim Legion and a route for the Suns of Couros to end her enmity. Ossegrahn blessed farmers and fishers and proposed a Conclave envoy to the Tchemetzi of Caitun.

n.Dawn: Rhianos was considering what Dawn might do to win their favour over the Eastern Sky and offered possible help tracking down Fortinbras, a Summer gift once earned by a hero of Dawn; Dawnish enchanters were invited to the parley.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page; its only possible link is Rhianos's refusal to help find the regalia of the first Empress, which the eternal said does not exist.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the civil servant Jorgen recalls having faced Jotun charges in his youth.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Jorgen recalls facing a Thule warlock, and Rhianos dismissed a request about the 'staves of power' of the Thule elite as not really a thing.
n.Wintermark: Sung specifically asked the Archmage of Night to bring the Shaman of Wintermark to the Friday-night parley on the mysteries of the Labyrinth, Freedom and the Shears.

t.Brocéliande: Rhianos had liked the idea of a statue watching over knights adventuring in Brocéliande, but their enthusiasm waned after the grand adventure there.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page, and no event there is described.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos's heralds hoped to hear what the three champions who represented their master in the tourney for patronage of the Icy Crag had done since.

Laid low.d: Before the assault the traitor Old Bushel Sykes helped the Jotun turn the Otterway into a major causeway, now finished, and spread anti-Imperial sentiment with stolen liao. The Jotun held back from invading Mitwold. The Strong Reeds and House Greywater then rose across Bregasland, aided by captains, beaters, Tom of Otterly and summoned Knights of Glory. Allied armies crossed from West Marsh and took Fisher's Rock. North Fens fell quickly and Grey Fens after harder fighting. The Empire also took the Rushes and parts of Ottermire, while the Jotun regrouped near Graven Rock. About four thousand fighters died, mostly Imperial. A Sentinel Gate conjunction offered a chance to defend House Greywater's estate from a Jotun band.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm's general notes that their sister legion is fighting the Druj in the Battens.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountains' general quotes Highborn siblings saying now is the time of miracles.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Tusks advanced from Graven March with a balanced strategy and supernatural clarity, and their scouts helped time the strike on Fisher's Rock. General Jakkan of the Fell Hammers made a point of seeking out the Imperial Orcs in battle.
n.Jotun: The Jotun completed the Otterway but chose not to invade Mitwold. They were then driven from both Fens, the Rushes and parts of Ottermire, and regrouped near Graven Rock. They fought to preserve their strength, and the Fell Hammers showed open disdain for the alliance with the Fishers.
n.Navarr: Isaella's Dance fought with envenomed weapons that killed swiftly, adding to the slaughter of Fishers and Jotun in the fens.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South marched to oust Mathilda Fisher and hunt Stephen of Sarcombe. The newly raised Burning Falcon blazed across the fens, and the Jotun eagerly sought them out after a century-old grudge.
n.The Marches: The Strong Reeds' uprising and the Drakes' assault helped return Bregasland to the Empire, and many wavering households welcomed the Marcher armies. Traitors such as Old Bushel Sykes, however, keep some Free Bregas support alive.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains fought in the vanguard against the yegarra, and the Summer Storm attacked from Kallavesa via Fisher's Rock. The Winterfolk fought honourably, suffered fewer deaths and claimed more ground.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was liberated and became an Imperial territory again, with the Senate to decide which nation receives it. Mathilda Fisher still lingers, rallying her remaining supporters to retreat.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Fisher storytellers praise those Fishers who fled to Hordalant as valiant heroes.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South's general vows to hunt Stephen of Sarcombe for fleeing Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa served as the launch point for the attack: the Summer Storm moved out from here, and allied armies crossed the river from West Marsh into Bregasland.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: with Liathaven under Jotun control, the Otterway may be meant to bring white granite into the fens for fortifications.
t.Mitwold: The Jotun did not invade Mitwold this season, but the Otterway is complete and the territory remains under threat.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Grey Fens was liberated after a more drawn-out fight, with the Fishers scattered and the Jotun driven back.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: North Fens fell almost at once, including Fisher's Rock. A Jotun band now threatens House Greywater's estate here, and the Strong Reeds' general has been asked to stop it through the Sentinel Gate.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: The Jotun had focused their work on the Otterway around Ottery and Sallow and fought more comfortably on Ottermire's firmer ground. The Empire occupied only parts of the region.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Imperial armies crossed the river from West Marsh to besiege Mathilda Fisher's forces at Fisher's Rock.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: With the Otterway completed before the Imperial assault, Oddmire is still under threat of Jotun invasion.

Pieces missing everywhere.d: Silas of the Cenotaph's mandate swelled congregations and stirred interest in a hugely ambitious construction at Bastion. Lady Josephine's mandate began changing Highborn attitudes towards lineaged, orcs and other sapient peoples. Jared's mandate let the Assembly support a chosen nation and respond to other assemblies' mandates. Urizen's Assembly had rejected such influence, and mandates were proposed in several nations to refuse or reciprocate Highborn aid. General Barachel arranged a meeting with the Vendarri on Greenstone Isle for nine Highborn, though the conjunction allowed fifteen, raising the possibility of betrayal. Asenath's Granite Pillar laid Aureli Major to rest, leaving only Clypion's miasma pillar for a possible Highborn mandate.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn Assembly's new outreach mandate cannot be used to contact the Dawnish in the Barrens.
n.Druj: Having been driven from Zenith, the Druj face Highborn efforts to destroy their remaining miasma pillar and holdouts in Clypion, and to win over their subjugated septs, beginning with the Vendarri.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: General Asenath hoped the Grendel would witness Imperial triumph; they are likely aware of it, but whether they were moved is impossible to tell.
n.Highguard: Highguard's people swelled their congregations, began to set aside prejudice against lineaged and orcs, and gained new Assembly powers. Its generals also created chances to contact Barrens septs and to destroy Zenith's last miasma pillar.
n.Imperial Orcs: Highborn attitudes towards the Imperial Orcs began to change as Lady Josephine's mandate urged citizens to renounce long-standing prejudice and judge by Virtue alone.
n.Navarr: Two mandates were proposed in the Navarr Assembly: Aneira Exiles End's would refuse further Highborn aid beyond the vallorn and City of Dreams, while Fintan Nighthaven's would seek to repay Highguard's sacrifice.
n.The League: The League Assembly faced rival mandates: Sofonisba Amilcara di Sarvos proposed refusing all Highborn aid, while Astrid Rezia Fjellrevening di Tassato proposed offering friendship and aid in return.
n.Urizen: Urizen, having rejected Highborn influence, could pass a mandate refusing all Highborn aid, or Tarquinius Ankarien's alternative to reciprocate; refusal would also block the Highborn mandate to destroy Clypion's pillar.
n.Varushka: Anastasiya Volkov proposed a mandate for the Varushkan Assembly to accept Highborn aid and offer aid in return, granting it the ability to respond to Highborn mandates.

t.Bastion: An appraisal by Eilian Sweetwater set out a hugely ambitious construction to make Bastion the indisputable centre of the Way. Highborn citizens could be persuaded to focus all their contributions on it.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's support for the Navarr attacking the vallorn in Brocéliande is cited as an example of Highborn loyalty.
t.The Barrens: General Barachel arranged a meeting with the treacherous Vendarri, and a Highborn mandate could open friendly contact with the Black Wind, the Karass or the Montanians.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the subjugated Barrens tribes lie on the far side of Therunin, too distant to witness the Granite Pillar's deeds in Zenith.
t.Zenith: The Granite Pillar laid Aureli Major and the tortured souls around two Druj spires to rest. Only the miasma pillar in Clypion now remains to be destroyed.

r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Greenstone Isle, in the mouth of the Greenstone estuary, was agreed as the site where nine Highborn could meet the Vendarri Pyroclast Garl Huonor and his ritualists.
r.Zenith/Clypion: Clypion holds Zenith's last miasma pillar. A Highborn mandate could send priests, alongside Urizeni sentinels and sword scholars, to destroy it with a powerful consecration.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Mentioned in passing: the Senate paid to tear down the miasma pillar in Iteri.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: Imperial heroes had already destroyed Lustri's miasma pillar, and General Asenath's orders proclaimed her stand there.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar destroyed the miasma pillar in Proceris.

Possibility days.d: The Conclave accepted the Brother of Wizards' offer. The Celestial Arch endowed crystal mana, and the League's Celestial Eclipse coven raised Penumbral Veils over Madruga and Segura, which the Eater of Secrets wove into a concealing fog. Imperial magicians met most arrivals, but many refugees fear priests, armoured knights, magistrates and militia, and some are surely Hand of Dumon cultists. Sephora of Sylaire gathered twenty potions as a bequest to the Conclave, and a group planned to visit Anvil. The Navarr Assembly could pass a mandate offering sanctuary in steadings and stridings, aiding integration but also helping malign wizards spread. Highguard had an alternative mandate. Otherwise the Suranni will form isolated enclaves.

n.Dawn: Many refugees are frightened of heavily armoured, heraldic figures such as knights of Dawn, and if left to themselves none will settle in Dawn for fear of priests and nobles who resemble Suranni knights.
n.Highguard: Exarch Luke proposed an alternative mandate urging Wayfarers and Magisters to welcome the Suranni, though its effect was uncertain and it would not see them settle in Highguard; the refugees fear cataphracts and Highborn priests.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: if the Navarr mandate passes, the refugees will settle in every corner of the Empire except among the Imperial Orcs.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Assembly had the opportunity to mandate that guides, vates and brands offer the Suranni sanctuary in their steadings and stridings, making most of them Navarr guests and aiding integration, at the risk of helping Hand of Dumon members and criminals spread across the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn magicians met refugees crossing into Madruga and Segura, but the Suranni distrust them because of the return of Arbonne's rebel slaves, and none will choose to settle in the Brass Coast.
n.The League: The League's Celestial Eclipse coven raised the veils that hid the refugees' flight, and affluent Suranni are eager to learn about the League, with some likely to form enclaves in Temeschwar and Holberg.
n.Urizen: Urizen's assembly invited the Suranni on condition they embrace the Way, an overture they mostly ignored, though many may still end up in Urizen and its northern reaches, and wealthier refugees show interest in the nation.
n.Varushka: Varushka's assembly welcomed the refugees but stressed virtue and the Way, which most rebuffed; nonetheless many Suranni are expected to settle in Varushka, either via the Navarr or in their own isolated villages.
n.Wintermark: Some refugees expressed interest in settling in Wintermark, and if left alone some will seek wild places there to found their own enclaves.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: few refugees wish to remain in territories bordering the Bay of Catazar.
t.Holberg: If the Suranni are left to their own devices, some will try to form enclaves in Holberg, hoping to blend into its crowded population.
t.Madruga: A Penumbral Veil raised over Madruga helped form the concealing fog, and many exhausted refugees, along with some more open-minded wizards, arrived here.
t.Sarvos: Some refugees reached the Empire by boat into Sarvos, including several of the more well-travelled, open-minded wizards.
t.Segura: A Penumbral Veil over Segura fed the protective fog, and many refugees crossed here, Sephora of Sylaire among the first to arrive and help liaise with Imperial magicians.
t.Shavronne: Mentioned in passing: the League magician Robert von Temeschwar was originally from Shavronne, rescued as a child from soldiers there.
t.Temeschwar: Robert von Temeschwar offered a band of refugees a home with his troupe in Temeschwar, and if left alone some Suranni will form enclaves in the city.

Rain king.d: Magical rains spread from Casinea, and every farm in a territory touched by the Hallow produced two extra drams of marrowort. Heralds offered to slowly upgrade standard farms for anyone who kept Blessing of New Spring cast through the year. They helped fight the blight in Madruga and gave arcane projections to the Sails of the First Flame, the Silver Chalice and the Marcher landskeepers. Ossegrahn proposed three commissions, each open until the end of the Autumn Equinox 385YE: the Houses of Healing, Winewater Hall and the Greenwatch. In return he hoped for amity, the shunning of Arhallogen, interdiction of venom magic, a Spring college and less killing in war.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a herald's quote says even the Druj can hope, and a Highborn magister notes that the anti-vallorn tools would also work against them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: an orc's quote recalls the Beoraidh arena and Mareave's Blood River, and warns against invading the Broken Shore.
n.Highguard: Ossegrahn offered the Greenwatch in Casinea, creating a Greenwatcher to be chosen unanimously by Highguard's senators from among Highborn citizens. Reikos's High Chalcis was also named as a possible site for the Houses of Healing.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage cited Tamazi support for the College of Warcasting in Skarsind as a model, which horrified the heralds, and an Imperial Orc oathwright is quoted on the Blood River.
n.Navarr: Heralds spoke with Navarr and Grey Pilgrims in Hercynia, Therunin and Miaren, and offered Winewater Hall, creating a Forestmender to be chosen unanimously by Navarr's senators to fight the vallorn.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Sails of the First Flame cast the Hallow, heralds helped against the blight in Madruga's Great Grasses, and Dhomiro Cassandra i Periera i Erigo received arcane projections from Lord Rain.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Ossegrahn permitted his arcane projections to be codified into Urizen lore as well as Imperial lore.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Greenwatch site in Mareholm lies on the border with Brocéliande, where it would watch over the vallorn.
t.Casinea: The gentle, magic-infused rains first fell over Casinea, and a Spring regio in Mareholm was proposed as the site of the Greenwatch.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: heralds of Ossegrahn visited the Navarr in Hercynia while discussing support against the vallorn.
t.Madruga: At the Archmage's request, heralds came to Madruga to help deal with the blight turning the Great Grasses to ash and sand, and they studied the Sails of the First Flame's healing magic there.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: an orc's quote explains that Mareave's Blood River is mine effluent, not blood.
t.Miaren: Chosen as the symbol of victory over the vallorn, Miaren is the proposed site of Winewater Hall, a gathering place for those fighting the vallorn without destructive magic.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Ossegrahn praised its practice of building defences instead of armies, and a herald urged the Empire to leave the people of Tsark alone.
t.Reikos: The Gardens of High Chalcis in Reikos, near a Spring regio, were one of two proposed sites for the Houses of Healing.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Tamazi support for the College of Warcasting in Skarsind was cited as a model, which the heralds found faintly horrifying.
t.Therunin: Heralds visited the Navarr here, and the Spring regio near Peakedge Stead was one of two proposed sites for the Houses of Healing.

r.Casinea/Mareholm: A nameless Spring regio among ancient hardwoods on the Brocéliande border was proposed as the site of the Greenwatch, which would cost 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial Orc's quote recalls being sent to the arena at Beoraidh.
r.Miaren/Greenfalls: The Winewater Spring here, a regio whose waters cleanse venom and poison, would be the foundation of the proposed Winewater Hall.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: The Spring regio near Peakedge Stead was proposed as a site for the Houses of Healing, which would create the Imperial title of Hand of the Healers.

Ratify treaty with Salt Lord Kaliact Spr.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Redoubt, the motion was presented as a treaty by the Ambassador to the Grendel and passed. According to Civil Service records, Salt Lord Kaliact agreed to cede Spiral and every holding within it to the Empire. In return, the Empire undertook to assign Spiral to the League and to allow those currently living there, orc and human alike, to become citizens. The ratification marked a negotiated, rather than military, return of Spiral to Imperial hands.

n.Grendel: Salt Lord Kaliact, dealing through the Imperial Ambassador to the Grendel, gave up Grendel control of Spiral and all its holdings in exchange for Imperial promises, including citizenship for the orcs living there.

t.Spiral: Spiral and all its holdings passed from Salt Lord Kaliact to the Empire, to be assigned to the League, and its current inhabitants, orc and human alike, were to be allowed to become citizens.

Rebuild Roads of Kahraman.d: Proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by Volodmartz, the commission passed at 200 thrones. It aimed to improve troop movement and defence, and promised reimbursement to Faraden families for their materials if trade ties were ever cut. The work needed 130 wains of white granite, 50 of weirwood and 45 thrones in labour over nine months, and could not progress while the Lasambrian Jotun had free access to Kahraman. Delara of the House of the Wanderer supplied most of the materials, with further contributions from the Bataguin Family and Vesna Borkovna Prochnost. Jotun disruption after the Autumn Equinox delayed completion, and raiders seized 10 wains of white granite, which had to be replaced.

n.Jotun: Lasambrian Jotun raiders delayed the project after the Autumn Equinox and seized 10 wains of white granite, and their free access to Kahraman was a condition that could halt the work entirely.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained repaired roads and a network of Kamkrag across one of their territories, improving defence and giving their citizens better access to abundant mines. The Bataguin Family helped pay for the work.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman's roads were rebuilt and Kamkrag were raised throughout the territory, despite Jotun raids that delayed the work and stole building materials.

Round here.d: Tamazi ritualists and a bonecarver came to discuss Worth with the Imperial Orcs. Janon's Flame of Virtue heralds, pleased with the Empire's war on slavery and the Druj, sought passionate citizens and named individuals. Evander and Associates returned with Axou concoctions, and the Alders-Baart family brought more cursed relics. A few Yerende from Solvihill travelled to Anvil, curious about the Rune of Blood. Abigail and Theodora Ashill sought to resolve a misunderstanding over Kleist's Winter Gardens. The Friends of Eduardo Boschetto attended a performance and sought exemplar recognition. Syrene's Wisdom, both Wayleaves, the Seer of the Spiral Sword and other titles were auctioned. Numerous national titles were set for appointment by vote.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Janon praised the Empire's commitment to destroying the Druj, and the Yerende are noted for generations of keeping secrets from them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the new Cerevado Nets were taken from under the nose of the Grendel governor of Feroz, and the Incarnadine Satchel has been missing since the occupation of Feroz.
n.Highguard: Highguard congregation leaders were to vote on who would become Bursar of the House of Spirits, able to purchase ilium from virtuous citizens.
n.Imperial Orcs: Tamazi ritualists sought the Imperial Orc camp to learn about Worth, Yerende visitors sought the orc enclave, and Janon's heralds asked for Imperial Orcs to speak about ending slavery. Orc unit commanders were also to appoint the Steel Fist, the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post, the Steward of the Mines of Gulhule and the Preceptor.
n.The League: League citizens could bid for the Regario Dossier and the Master of the Imperial Mint, and League business owners were to appoint the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild. League affairs also featured the Kleist's Winter Gardens dispute and the Friends of Eduardo Boschetto's bid to have him recognised as an exemplar.
n.The Marches: A small group of Marcher traders, possibly linked to Sweetroot in Upwold, grumbled that buying Axou concoctions over homegrown narcotics showed a lack of Pride in the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens who own mana sites were to appoint the Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks, who purchases white granite from Axou traders.
n.Varushka: Varushkan mine and forest owners were to appoint the Gift of the Dwindling Star, the Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks and the first Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark military unit owners were to appoint the Talon of Kauppahall, a merchant able to buy ilium and white granite from the virtuous.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the roads of Casinea were busy with merchants, traders and peddlers heading to Anvil for the summit.
t.Feroz: The new Cerevado Nets had been taken from the old Scorrero Nets under the Grendel governor's nose, and the Vizier of the Incarnadine Satchel remained custodian of a satchel missing since Feroz's occupation.
t.Holberg: Plans to protect the cursed Duelling Grounds of Holmauer Park as Kleist's Winter Gardens stalled over whether they should benefit Holberg directly or be auctioned for the Senate, prompting the Ashills to come to Anvil to seek a resolution.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is not named on the page; its only apparent link is the Highguard title Bursar of the House of Spirits, appointed this season.
t.Ossium: The Yerende are noted as having left Ossium at the Empire's invitation, and Varushkans were to appoint the first Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the late actor Cosmo had dropped the appellation "von Sarvos", and Boschetto once flooded a theatre staging The Sail of Sarvos.
t.Skarsind: A small group of Yerende orcs set out from Skarsind towards Anvil, a sign their reticence may be thawing.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Seer of the Spiral Sword title, granting custodianship of the only Imperial runeforge, was auctioned this season.
t.Tassato: Tassato's theatre world mourned the infamous impresario Eduardo Boschetto, whose friends travelled to Anvil to honour him and seek his recognition as an exemplar of Ambition.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Yerende travellers were seen heading east on the Temeschwar trod towards Anvil.
t.Upwold: Marcher traders who may be associated with the market town of Sweetroot complained that Imperial buyers preferred foreign Axou concoctions to homegrown narcotics.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: The first Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore was to be appointed by Varushkan mine and forest owners, gaining the ability to buy metals and forest resources from the docks at Kostjyas Respite.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Yerende living quietly on farmland in a valley north of Solvihill, growing orcsroot and herbs, sent a few of their number to Anvil.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named; the only Upwold reference is Marcher traders possibly linked to Sweetroot grumbling about Axou concoctions.

Shallow days.d: The Salt Lords sent a formal delegation to meet Ambassador Abel at the Senate on Friday evening, proposing their customary exchange of written opening offers; any treaty would need ratifying by both sides. The Golden Winds stayed off Necropolis, and a second navy, the Tempest, sheltered between Mudport and Siroc. Highguard and Freeborn Synod mandates were offered that could earn local businesses extra income, or, in Highguard's case, condemn such trade. The Cerevado Nets were established, and an enraged Rahab was barred from retaliating. Grendel Questioners of Cunning sought to debate priests of Wisdom. An unnamed Spiral figure asked to meet seven named citizens in Outer Anvil.

n.Grendel: The Council of Salt Lords sent diplomats to open treaty talks and kept two navies in Imperial waters to trade. Rahab was forbidden to retaliate over the lost nets, while Questioners and a Spiral dignitary pursued their own meetings at Anvil.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly faced two competing mandates: one fully endorsing trade with the Grendel navy off Necropolis, and one from Eli of the Cenotaph condemning it. The earlier, heavily caveated judgement had persuaded only a few traders.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained the new Cerevado Nets, whose custodian the fleet captains would choose. The Tempest's arrival near Madruga gave the Freeborn Assembly the chance to mandate profitable trade with the Grendel.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to the Grendel, Abel, is identified as being of Urizen.

t.Feroz: Governor Rahab was furious at the theft of the Scorrero Nets but barred by the treaty and the Salt Lords from striking back. Meanwhile, work to fortify the walls of Oran was already half-finished.
t.Madruga: The Grendel navy Tempest anchored between Mudport and Siroc to resupply and trade. A Freeborn mandate could give every business in Madruga 2 extra crowns while the navy remained.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the North Mareave Trading Consortium is rumoured as one possible power behind the Spiral dignitary seeking a meeting at Anvil.
t.Necropolis: The Golden Winds remained moored off the coast without hostile action. A Highborn mandate could give each business 2 extra crowns, while a rival mandate would condemn all trade with the Grendel there.
t.Segura: The Cerevado Nets were established, with a new Bourse seat upriver at Cerevado and ilium already being gathered. The Tempest sheltered in waters between Mudport and Siroc.
t.Spiral: A Grendel merchant from Spiral, perhaps a leader of a powerful faction or someone from Salt Lord Kaliact's court, sent Graime the Questioner to arrange an exclusive meeting in Outer Anvil. Whether Kaliact's representatives would join the treaty delegation remained unclear.
t.Tathar: Mentioned in passing: Tathar is not named directly, and is touched on only through the wider Grendel treaty talks.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Grendel began reinforcing the walls of the town of Oran shortly after the Winter Solstice. The work was already half-complete, probably with Autumn magic, and it was unclear who was paying for it.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Mentioned in passing: Apulus is not named directly, and is touched on only through the rumours about powerful Spiral factions seeking contact with the Empire.

Support Expansion of Caitun.d: Proposed by the Senator for Kallavesa and seconded by the Senator for Mitwold, the motion backed the expansion described in the Butterfly in Reverse Wind of Fortune. It passed at a cost of 70 thrones. The Empire was to supply 15 wains of weirwood plus 45 crowns in transport costs, with the work taking six months. After the Spring Equinox, Rane Shardbearer provided the weirwood and Fancy Jack contributed 5 thrones 5 crowns. The expansion was completed. From the Autumn Equinox 385YE Imperial fleets could trade at Caitun, and Wintermark, Marcher and Freeborn fleets could hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow.

n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Senator for Kallavesa proposed the motion, and once the expansion was complete Wintermark fleets gained the ability to hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow from the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

t.Sea of Snow: The completed expansion of Caitun opened the Sea of Snow to monster hunting by Wintermark, Marcher and Freeborn fleets from the Autumn Equinox 385YE.

The falling sky.d: Axos refused to send delegates until its dispute with the Empire was resolved. The Commonwealth and Sumaah asked to postpone the Pact meeting to the Summer Solstice. The Commonwealth claimed the Tears of the Moon in Rachensgrab and welcomed gifts of mithril, weirwood or white granite. A Grendel force torched Issyk's docks, and the Eastern Broker lost or downgraded Axou trade ministries. After Asavea's declaration of war, unconfirmed rumours told of warships striking Sarvos, Siroc or Trivento. The Sarcophan opened Betovering Docks to Imperial fleets and urged the Gjullit to keep their Pallas Docks offer open. Merchant-prince Vito Danierri de Sarvos offered to carry ambassadors' letters unread.

n.Grendel: A large Grendel force sacked Issyk's docks, looting warehouses and burning the piers, apparently in anger at Axou sanctions and Axos siding with the Empire. The raid damaged Imperial trade with the Axou.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Felix's Watch of Highguard is named as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Pakt of the Imperial Orcs is named as Ambassador to Asavea, the nation now at war with the Empire.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Nighthaven of Navarr is named as Ambassador to Axos, whose people are boycotting the Liberty Pact meeting and refusing to send delegates.
n.The League: League lands were at the centre of rumours of an Asavean naval attack on Sarvos or Trivento. Sarcophan families showed interest in the idle Cavabianca Docks, and Vito Danierri de Sarvos of the Golden Sugar cartel offered to carry ambassadors' letters. Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato is named as Ambassador to the Commonwealth.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the neighbouring nations whose closeness gives them outsized influence over the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Thalia of Netherwatch, Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves, persuaded the Sarcophan to have the Gjullit keep their Pallas Docks offer open another season. Ariadne of Urizen is named as Ambassador to Jarm, which has severed ties with the Empire.

t.Bay of Catazar: In the islands of Rachensgrab, the Commonwealth has claimed the Tears of the Moon and is working with freed former slaves to restore order. It has asked wealthy Imperials for gifts of mithril, weirwood or white granite to help rebuild.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named among the smaller neighbouring nations that hold unexpected influence over the Empire.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was among the places rumoured to have been struck by Asavean warships, though no reports were confirmed. The merchant-prince Vito Danierri de Sarvos offered to carry ambassadors' letters abroad.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the page refers readers to opportunities concerning Faraden that arose from the Sea of Snow mapping expedition.

The troubled words.d: Achille di Sarvos commissioned the Holberg Scholars of the Sword Academy, with the Master of Defence as custodian. The Urizen Assembly announced that Cato Hypation and Clytemnestra would teach there, and other sword scholars followed. The League Assembly could enact a mandate urging bravos to remember Alexander von Holberg and embrace the philosophy, or Erasmo di Tassato's variant invoking Emperor Frederick and calling for more teachers. Either would raise the Master's stipend by a third and spark political interest among bravos. Opposing mandates would curtail the Academy's cultural influence and cut its income by a third. If nothing is done, sword scholar ideas will slowly spread. The Lepidean Librarian might commission research into Alexander.

n.The League: The League Assembly faces a choice over whether Holberg's bravos should embrace sword scholar philosophy and the legacy of Alexander von Holberg, risking a radical, Synod-sceptical movement, or reject it to preserve tradition.
n.Urizen: Urizeni sword scholars, led by Cato Hypation and Clytemnestra, have taken up teaching in Holberg, offering a chance to spread their philosophy of independence from the Synod beyond Urizen.

t.Holberg: Holberg hosts the new sword academy, and its bravos may embrace or reject the sword scholars' teachings, either igniting a philosophical and political renaissance or confining the Academy to mere swordsmanship.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: renewed interest in the inspiration of Ratibor of Temeschwar is cited as a reason opposition to the Synod may arise sooner.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Clytemnestra's defence of threatening to dissolve the Citadel Guard is cited as having forced the Empire to free Zenith.

Time and time again.d: Ruined roads have crippled army movement between Braydon's Jasse, Serra Briante and Serra Damata, and fortifications now defend only their own region. Raiders cut Damatian Cliffs output by 7 wains and the Great Mine of Briante by 6. The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills and the Mistress of the Dust Parador lost their top two ministry ranks. The options set out were: Senate-funded mercenaries at 10 thrones a season; a repair folly costing 70 white granite, 50 weirwood and 240 crowns over nine months; Faraden Kamkrag towers part-funded by the Bataguin; and help from Commonwealth engineers working with an Imperial army. Two Sentinel Gate conjunctions targeted Jotun bands led by Jarl Thraggan and Venator.

n.Jotun: Some forty thousand Jotun arrived after the Winter Solstice, hold Braydon's Jasse and are pushing into the Jade Range, where bands under Jarl Thraggan and the herald Venator threaten mining families and Dawnish yeofolk.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn of Kahraman face lost mine and quarry output, weakened ministries and feuding families, though the proposed Kamkrag would add two ingots a season to every Freeborn mine in the territory.
n.The League: League mercenaries could be hired by the Senate to guard Kahraman's caravans, and League military units would gain a lucrative Kahraman Caravan Guards adventure if the Senate paid for it.

t.Kahraman: The territory's sabotaged roads, raided caravans and reduced Bourse output are the subject of the appraisal, which offers costed plans to repair the roads and build Faraden-style Kamkrag watchtowers across the territory.
t.Madruga: Kahraman's caravans are now forced to detour south-east through Madruga, where orc raiders prey on them, and the Commonwealth Embassy there has offered the Baumeister engineers to help rebuild the roads.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Towers of Anduz that protect merchants visiting Segura are noted as having been inspired by Faraden Kamkrag.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: mithril and white granite caravans can no longer take their old direct routes to Tassato.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Jotun invaded and now control Braydon's Jasse, so road repairs can be started but not finished until they are driven out, and Fort Braydon's protection no longer reaches neighbouring regions.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Dust Parador stands here and the Jotun are advancing on it, while two Sentinel Gate conjunctions sent heroes against Jarl Thraggan's band near the Liscano family and against Venator on the Sylvan Track.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The Great Mine of Briante loses 6 wains of mithril a season to raiders, and armies can no longer move freely between Serra Briante and its neighbouring regions.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Damatian Cliffs lose 7 wains of white granite a season to raids, and the ruined roads cut Serra Damata off from Serra Briante for armies and fortification support.

Tooth by tooth.d: Ubarius's statement passed the Pride Assembly at Winter 384YE by 285 to 26. It warned that growing numbers of foreigners were settling in the Empire without adopting the Way. Each summit until the end of Winter 385YE, the Cardinal of Pride could submit a mandate, using 75 doses of liao, to send priests to learn the beliefs of a named group. This would yield understanding rather than conversions. The civil service suggested the Faraden, Feni, Great Forest Orcs, hylje, Marracossans, Montanians, Sand Fishers and the septs of Skarsind, and warned that targeting the Axos would fail. Under Cardinal Harwyn Eternal, missions went to the Faraden in Spring, the hylje in Summer and the Great Forest Orcs in Autumn. The last was cut short by events in the Barrens.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but unspecified events in the Barrens cut short the Autumn mission to the Great Forest Orcs.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel's claim to have been brought to the Way by Urizeni missionaries over a century ago is cited as a past success.
n.Imperial Orcs: The four septs living in Skarsind were a possible missionary target, but the civil service warned that a careless approach could upset delicate negotiations with them.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun thralls in the Marches are listed among non-believers, and the conversion of the Lasambrians is said to have benefited the Jotun more than the Empire.
n.Navarr: The Montanians of Therunin, some of whom roam the trods with the Great Forest Orcs, were offered as a possible target, though their embrace of Freedom makes them hard to reconcile with the Way.
n.The Brass Coast: The Marracossans of Trajadoz in Madruga were a possible target, though the cession of that town would limit the Empire's legal recourse if they responded badly; the story is set among Freeborn in a parador in Sobral.
n.The League: The Sand Fishers settled near Holberg, the Empire's greatest recent success in spreading the Virtues, were named as an easier group to approach.
n.The Marches: The Jotun thralls of the Mournwold are named among non-believers in the Empire and as a possible target whose scattered beliefs could be collated and published.
n.Wintermark: At the Summer Solstice the Assembly sent Eska Crowspeaker to urge a mission to Wintermark's hylje allies, producing startling insights into their spiritual beliefs.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the various foreign enclaves and embassies in the Bay's territories are cited as examples of non-believers in the Empire.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean temple to the Black Bull built in Feroz is cited as a cautionary example.
t.Holberg: The Sand Fishers living in the marshy forests on Holberg's edge, favourably inclined to the Empire and the Virtues, were proposed as a likely easy target for missionaries.
t.Madruga: The Marracossans of Trajadoz, newly ceded as an independent enclave, were expected to build a temple to their gods and were listed as a risky missionary target.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold thralls were suggested as a group whose already known beliefs missionaries could gather and publish.
t.Skarsind: The Ethengraw, Illarawm, Yerende and Tamazi septs of Skarsind could be approached, but only at the risk of disturbing precarious negotiations.
t.The Barrens: The Great Forest Orcs of Peytaht were the Autumn target, but events in the Barrens cut the mission short after it learned only something of their beliefs about the Great Forest.
t.Therunin: The Montanians living in Therunin, remnants of the Freedom Heresy, were named as a possible target whose devotion to Freedom complicates any reconciliation with the Way.

Underwater sunshine.d: Kostjyas Respite, built under an Imperial Wayleave, raised taxation by 5 thrones a season in every Imperial territory bordering the Semmerlak except Holberg, where the Sand Fishers hold Misericorde. Civil servants are drawing up proposals for further ports. Dho'uala's tithe brought disappearances, including all aboard the Dawnish ship Lady Celementine, and gave Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets a production penalty. Cerulean Mazzarine and ilium prices rose. Monstrous beavers tried to dam rivers in Ossium and Semmerholm but were defeated. Dreams at the Maze of Zoriah warned that something tied to the Semmerlak would happen at Anvil during the Hour of Smoke.

n.Dawn: Dawnish lake shores share in the port's economic boom, but Dawnish fleets suffer Dho'uala's tithe, cursed flotsam has harmed beachcombers, and the Lady Celementine was found emptied of every soul aboard.
n.The League: Holberg gains nothing from the new port's trade because the Sand Fishers control Misericorde, yet its fleets still suffer the production penalty and its sailors are among the vanished.
n.Varushka: Varushka completed both the Iron Roads and Kostjyas Respite, but its fleets and lakeside ministries now suffer from Dho'uala's wrath, and its heroes fought off beaver horrors in Ossium.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the lost Lady Celementine was carrying Dawnish silk, wine and bread from Astolat.
t.Holberg: Holberg is the one lakeside territory without a tax increase, though a dock in Misericorde or Utterlund might be possible, and its traders and treasure hunters have fallen victim to the lake's disappearances.
t.Karov: Karov's taxation rises by 5 thrones a season and civil servants are preparing proposals to improve it, but the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak faces less available ilium at a higher price.
t.Karsk: Karsk gains the 5-throne tax increase and is included in the civil service's prosperity proposals, while the Ketsov Mir Mozga shrug off the lake's troubles and their deals are unaffected.
t.Miekarova: Pilgrims at the Maze of Zoriah in Miekarova have dreamt of weasels and otters warning that Dho'uala is roused and something will happen at Anvil.
t.Ossium: Ossium is now home to Kostjyas Respite, which ends its extra building costs, and its flooding has subsided after Varushkan heroes destroyed beaver horrors damming the Lanit River.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's taxation rises and proposals to improve it are under way, but cursed objects have washed up on its beaches and beaver horrors flooded the land near Semmer's Rose until House Tamerlaine's knights destroyed them.
t.The Semmerlak: The sovereign Dho'uala has stirred in the depths, bringing strange lights, torn nets, stolen cargo and vanished sailors to the lake's waters.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater gains the 5-throne tax increase and is included in the port proposals, though cursed objects have washed up on its beaches and weirwood traders may prefer the road past Sentinel's Folly to the lake.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Sand Fisher control of Misericorde keeps Holberg from the new trade; a Sand Fisher raft vanished, leaving only a splintered spearhead on its beach, and a dock here is a possibility.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Mentioned in passing: Utterlund is named as a possible site for a new dock to spread Holberg's wealth across the Semmerlak.
r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Since the Maze of Zoriah in Mieriada was consecrated with true liao, its pilgrims have had lucid dreams of speaking animals warning of Dho'uala and the Hour of Smoke.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Bittershore is no longer under-developed now that Kostjyas Respite's docks are open, and its first Merchant Boyar is due to be appointed at the Spring Equinox.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Mentioned in passing: the Drownbark Forest's marshes were at risk of damage had the beaver horrors' dam on the Lanit River not been stopped.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Varushkan heroes stopped beaver horrors damming the Lanit River in Nearweald, and the vanished Lady Celementine was carrying spear-tips for the fortified barracks there.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Mentioned in passing: Sandling is not named, but it is tied to Weirwater's Semmerlak shoreline, where cursed objects washed ashore and the tax boom applies.

Where do we go from here?.d: Following Naomi of Virtue's Rest's proposal of three great commissions, the Master of the Koboldi commissioned the Crucible of Fate, restoring and expanding the forges of Spire Calator near Mount Lutum, long home to ushabti artisans. The Urizen Assembly may now pass one of two competing mandates, emphasising function or form, to embrace the Crucible and end Zenith's despair. The koboldi built themselves quarters beneath the spire, and Adamant has asked the Conclave to decide by declaration of Concord whether they may stay. The Radix of Truth and Eye of the Heavens remain possible. Parts imported from the League earned every League business owner a share of 140 ingots.

n.Druj: The Druj's desolation of Zenith left it bereft of hope, and their marauders still roam there, but the Crucible offers Urizen a way to shed their awful legacy.
n.The League: League workshops, notably the Wunderkind of Holberg, supplied the cogs, gears and instruments for the Crucible, and every League citizen owning a business received a share of a one-off payment of 140 ingots.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly can now choose between mandates championing function or form to embrace the Crucible of Fate and give Zenith a new destiny, while still able to pursue the Radix of Truth or Eye of the Heavens.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Wunderkind of Holberg are named as excelling at the fine clockwork parts imported for the Crucible.
t.Zenith: The Crucible of Fate stands complete in Zenith, and an Assembly mandate embracing it would end the territory's despair, though tortured souls, Druj marauders and realm monsters still remain to be dealt with.

r.Zenith/Iteri: The page names no specific region; Spire Calator near Mount Lutum, site of the newly restored Crucible and the koboldi's hidden quarters, is the focus within Zenith.

You can't count on me.d: The Imperial Crown remained interdicted because its reconciliation was declared in an 'emergency session' with no legal standing. The Prefect would propose a Declaration of License, and if it failed the magistrates would seize and destroy the Crown. A Summer boon linked to Barien inspired crafting across the Mournwold and promised a trade boon. The Civil Service named Hammare 'Meathammer' Stenning Custodian of the Lost, and Harad of the High Path's Quiet Hall in Oakways was offered for Endowment. Tharim warded the Hall of Worlds while his image is displayed. Barien's heralds, Surut's agent and Zakalwe's strategy game awaited citizens. Dawn's Eastern Sky moved towards becoming a favoured army.

n.Dawn: Five Summer eternals stood ready to patronise the Eastern Sky under Dame Aurum de Castellan, and Cathan Canae offered her favour if a Synod mandate barred Dawnish generals from giving ground in defence. Barien's heralds would hold court at House du Lac, and Zakalwe invited six Dawnish strategists to a game.
n.Druj: A Penumbral Veil still hung over the Druj-held Barrens, and the Dripping Echoes of the Fen were raised in Ossium in case the Druj tried to reclaim the land.
n.Highguard: A new shroud was raised over the Highborn territory of Necropolis, frustrating any scrying into it.
n.Navarr: The late Navarr magician Harad of the High Path left his Quiet Hall in Oakways as a bequest. The Conclave could endow it to the Custodian of the Lost as a hospital, or to his niece Mathoni High Path in exchange for 5 measures of dragonbone each season.
n.The Brass Coast: New shrouds were raised over the Freeborn territories of Madruga and Segura. Barien's heralds also held a challenge scroll for Tono Shartha Riqueza.
n.The League: A Penumbral Veil continued to hang over the League territory of Sarvos.
n.The Marches: A Summer enchantment over the Mournwold inspired Marchers in crafting, cooking and brewing and promised a season of thriving trade. A Spring wall rose in Alderly, and Marchers were called to bring rough music against the stubborn ghosts of Greensward.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Crown was recovered from the Thule by private collectors.
n.Urizen: The Custodian of the Lost carried on the legacy of Zenith's destroyed Spire of Twisting Shadows, and the Spire of the Seventh Mist pressed on with its campaign for access to the Brilliant Star mine. Zenith gained nightwoven fortifications and a Spring wall in Lustri while remaining veiled.
n.Varushka: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in Drownbark Forest in Ossium to shield the Iron Helms against any Druj attempt to retake the land.
n.Wintermark: Fog fortifications were raised over Kallavesa Marsh and West Marsh. The Civil Service ruled that the Wintermark coven the Saque Magique could not hold the Custodian title and named Hammare 'Meathammer' Stenning instead.

t.Kallavesa: Magical fog fortifications lay heavy over Kallavesa Marsh and West Marsh.
t.Madruga: A new shroud was raised over Madruga, blocking divination into the territory unless it is pierced.
t.Miaren: Harad's Quiet Hall in Oakways became a bequest the Conclave could endow, either as a hospital for magical maladies or to Mathoni High Path for its dragonbone.
t.Mournwold: A Summer enchantment linked to Barien filled the Mournwold with inspired craft, food and drink, promising a three-month boom in trade. The territory also gained magical fortifications, while ghosts lingered in Greensward.
t.Necropolis: A new shroud was raised over Necropolis, hindering any scrying into the territory.
t.Ossium: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen were raised in Drownbark Forest to protect the Iron Helms.
t.Sarvos: A Penumbral Veil continued to hang over Sarvos.
t.Segura: A new shroud was raised over Segura, blocking divination into the territory.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: a statue honouring Eleonaris at the Golden Causeway in Semmerholm secured her favour for the Eastern Sky.
t.The Barrens: A Penumbral Veil still hung over the Barrens, frustrating Imperial scrying.
t.Zenith: Nightwoven fortifications strengthened Zenith's mists and a Spring wall rose in Lustri, while a veil remained over the territory. The legacy of its destroyed Spire of Twisting Shadows was clarified.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Magical fog fortifications were raised over Kallavesa Marsh.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Magical fog fortifications were raised over West Marsh.
r.Miaren/Oakways: Harad's Quiet Hall, a wayhouse in idyllic woodland rich in dragonbone, awaited the Conclave's decision on whether it would become a hospital or pass to his niece's family.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: A great wall of branch and thicket was summoned from the Spring realm in Alderly.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Greensward remained haunted, with stubborn ghosts gathered at Overton Ruins. Mary Overton called for Marchers to confront them with rough music through a Sentinel Gate conjunction.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in Drownbark Forest to shield the Iron Helms against the Druj.
r.Zenith/Lustri: A great wall of branch and thicket was summoned from the Spring realm in Lustri.

You do it to yourself.d: Fintan Nighthaven's mandate (1594 to 367) rejected the false virtues behind "Death to the Druj", while Lenarius Ankarien's call to exterminate the Druj by any means narrowly failed (739 to 793). The Urizen and Vigilance Assemblies passed statements urging that the Druj legacy be scoured from Zenith. With Ossium liberated, the Barrens poised to fall and the Spires of Dusk taken, Lady Laudine of House duLac's wording would make the Druj war the priority for a year, whatever the sacrifice. Mael Donjeon's competing wording would refuse that priority and leave the Military Council and Senate free to agree terms with the Druj. Only one can be enacted. New answers would first need a statement of principle.

n.Druj: The Druj are described as uniquely cruel and now on the run. The Synod must choose whether the Empire pursues all-out victory over them or treats them as just one enemy, potentially open to negotiated terms.
n.Grendel: Under the Laudine mandate, talks with the Grendel could involve sacrifices for the sake of the Druj war. Under the Donjeon mandate, their navy and allies are cited as a greater threat, and Feroz and Spiral are noted as languishing under Grendel rule.
n.Jotun: The Wintermark campaign against the Jotun is described as honourable. Prioritising the Druj could mean sacrifices in that war, while the opposing view points out that the Jotun field more armies than the Mallum.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: only against the Navarr does the Jotun war turn to savagery, with neither side able to tolerate the other's existence.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are said to honour the Marchers in their own way, and Jarl Kierheim's vow concerning the Jotun failure in the Mournwold is quoted.
n.Thule: The Thule are said to keep their word, and the costly peace with them has held. Under the Laudine mandate, talks with them could also involve sacrifices to focus on the Druj.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly passed a statement urging Sword Scholars to scour the remnants of the Druj from Zenith. The opening story follows the Urizen sentinel Belisar and the scout Philamon, a veteran of Morrow and Zenith.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is cited as the first territory liberated from the Druj and now a thriving territory of Varushka.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermarkers are credited with leading an honourable campaign against the Jotun. Sermersuaq is cited as nearly lost for a generation, regained only through the Thule alliance.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: cited as languishing under Grendel rule, part of the price of the Empire's focus on the Druj.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the scout Philamon is said to have fought in Morrow.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Kierheim vows the Jotun will not make peace until all shamed by their failure in the Mournwold have passed on.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: noted as the first territory liberated from the Druj and now a thriving part of Varushka.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the northern lands under the Dragons of Otkodov are described as the price paid for the Thule alliance.
t.Sarangrave: Imperial spies have scouted the Sarangrave for its secrets and weaknesses, and raising a rebellion there is judged difficult but not impossible.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: cited as nearly lost for a generation and returned to Imperial rule only through the alliance with the Thule.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: cited alongside Feroz as languishing under Grendel rule.
t.The Barrens: The Druj armies have been mauled and defeated here, and the territory looks set to fall to the Empire soon.
t.Zenith: The Druj have fled Zenith but left deep scars. The Urizen and Vigilance Assemblies passed statements urging citizens to root out the Druj legacy and stay watchful, though no military threat currently faces the territory.
